titel: Circulating Current in Conductor Line of Open-Circuit after Semiconductor Device Turn-Off
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT For example, a semiconductor element is turned off in a power supply circuit. A part of the circuit becomes an open‐circuit. The magnetic energy stored by the parasitic inductance of the conductor line in the open‐circuit is then released as circulating currents flowing within the conductor line. The circulating current flows symmetrically between the left and right sides of the conductor line, which is divided into two parts widthwise. The author clarified this circulating current by measuring the local magnetic field on the conductor line using the optical probe type magnetic field sensor. In addition, this paper describes in detail the current density distribution and the magnetic field of the circulating current in conductor lines of various cross‐sectional shapes. The analysis results revealed that the integrated current density within the conductor line is zero regardless of the cross‐sectional shape of the conductor line, but circulating currents flow. Also the magnetic field around a highly symmetric cylindrical conductor line is zero. On the other hand, the magnetic field increases as the aspect ratio increases, as in the case of a less symmetrical rectangular conductor line.

titel: A novel frameshift variant in TTC29 associated with total asthenozoospermia and male infertility
ort: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
zusammenfassung: Background Severe sperm motility defects are an important cause of male infertility and are frequently associated with sperm flagellar abnormalities. TTC29 encodes an evolutionarily conserved axonemal protein implicated in sperm flagellar assembly and motility, yet the pathogenic mechanisms of TTC29 variants remain incompletely understood. Methods A Chinese man with total asthenozoospermia was investigated using whole-exome sequencing, Sanger sequencing, transmission electron microscopy, sperm immunofluorescence, and heterologous expression analysis in HEK293 T cells. The clinical outcome following intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) was also evaluated. Results Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel TTC29 frameshift variant (NM_031956.4:c.121dupA; p. Ile41Asnfs*21), which was confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Transmission electron microscopy revealed severe ultrastructural abnormalities involving both the midpiece and principal piece, with disruption of the canonical 9 + 2 axonemal architecture and marked abnormalities of peri-axonemal structures. In representative immunofluorescence images, TTC29 signal was readily detected along the sperm flagellum in the fertile control, whereas a visibly weaker signal was observed in spermatozoa from the proband. Heterologous expression analysis showed little or no detectable production of the expected TTC29 protein product from the mutant construct. Although fertilization was achieved following two ICSI cycles, no clinical pregnancy was obtained. Conclusion We identified a novel TTC29 frameshift variant associated with total asthenozoospermia and male infertility. Genetic, ultrastructural, and heterologous expression evidence supports a deleterious effect of the identified TTC29 variant, thereby expanding the mutational spectrum of TTC29 -related infertility and providing further insight into the molecular basis of severe sperm motility disorders.

titel: Radiologically suspected catheter-related septic subclavian thrombophlebitis presenting as a rapidly progressive cervical abscess in a hemodialysis patient: a fatal case report
zusammenfassung: Abstract Introduction Central venous catheters remain widely used for haemodialysis (HD) access, particularly in patients who lack suitable permanent vascular access. Although catheter-related infections are well recognized, severe deep neck infections secondary to catheter-associated septic thrombophlebitis are rarely reported. Case description We report the case of a 75-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease on long-term HD who presented with a rapidly enlarging painful right cervical swelling. His medical history included multiple failed arteriovenous fistulas and repeated central venous catheterizations for dialysis access. Physical examination revealed a firm erythematous cervical mass without airway compromise. Laboratory investigations demonstrated marked leukocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the neck showed a large cervical collection with internal gas and rim enhancement consistent with a deep abscess. Imaging also demonstrated thrombosis of the right subclavian vein raising suspicion for septic thrombophlebitis, along with extensive surrounding inflammatory changes and gas tracking toward adjacent osseous structures mainly the sternoclavicular joint, raising suspicion for emphysematous osteomyelitis. The patient was started on broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and underwent urgent surgical drainage of the abscess. Anticoagulation therapy was initiated for the associated septic venous thrombosis. Despite aggressive medical and surgical management, the patient’s condition deteriorated rapidly and he died several days later due to overwhelming infection. Discussion Presumed catheter-related septic thrombophlebitis can lead to devastating complications including deep cervical infection and possible emphysematous osteomyelitis. This case highlights the importance of early recognition of unusual infectious complications of long-term dialysis catheters and underscores the need for vigilance in patients with repeated vascular access interventions. titel: Arabidopsis bZIP68 Modulates Flowering Time Potentially with Chromatin and Stress-Responsive Regulators
zusammenfassung: In Arabidopsis thaliana, the physiological functions and regulatory network of the transcription factor bZIP68 remain poorly understood. To investigate its potential functions and regulome, we integrated multiple publicly available omics datasets, including protein–protein interaction and co-expression networks, transcriptomic data from bzip68 mutants, bZIP68 ChIP-seq data, and ChIP-seq/DAP-seq and transcriptomic datasets for candidate regulatory factors. These integrated analyses suggested that bZIP68 is involved in floral morphology, flowering regulation, and responses to abiotic stress. Notably, SWI3D, MINU2, and CAMTA1 were identified as highly probable components of the bZIP68 core regulome. Subsequent transcriptomic network analysis revealed their putative signaling cascades. To validate the predicted role of bZIP68 in flowering regulation, we analyzed five independent homozygous EMS mutant (HEM) lines. All five mutant lines exhibited altered flowering phenotypes compared to the wild type. In conclusion, this study establishes an integrative framework for identifying the bZIP68 regulatory network and uncovers its novel physiological role in modulating flowering.

titel: Mechanical performance of hybrid lignin/glass fibre epoxy bio-composites
zusammenfassung: Hybrid bio-composites integrating renewable lignin and synthetic glass fibres have emerged as sustainable alternatives to traditional composites, addressing the environmental concerns associated with non-degradable synthetic materials. This study investigates the synergistic effects of lignin and glass fibres on the mechanical properties of glass fibre-reinforced polymer composites (GFRPs). Composite samples were fabricated with varying weight percentages of lignin (0%, 2%, 4%, and 6%) and glass fibres (1%, 2%, and 3%), adhering to ASTM standards for tensile, bending, and impact tests. The findings reveal that lignin significantly enhances the tensile and bending properties at optimal concentrations. However, excessive lignin (>4 wt%) reduces the composite's performance due to interface disruptions. Flexural strength exhibited a similar trend, with a peak at lower lignin concentrations. Numerical simulations using ABAQUS software showed good agreement with experimental results, validating the computational approach. The results of this study demonstrate that lignin can serve as an effective reinforcing agent in hybrid composites, improving mechanical properties while reducing environmental problems.

titel: Biological Products Precondition Field Soil and Induce Changes in Bacterial Communities to Reduce Root‐Knot Nematode Symptoms in Tomato Crops
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT Root‐knot nematodes ( Meloidogyne spp., RKNs) cause significant yield losses in tomato crops and current chemical control methods have limitations. For example, the use of nematicides have associated safety concerns for both environmental and human health. Some biological products are promising sustainable alternatives to chemicals. The present study investigated whether field application of selected biological products could precondition the soil, altering bacterial communities, which in turn could reduce Meloidogyne javanica infestation of tomatoes in the greenhouse. Soil was collected from a tomato field site where commercially available biological products, Popul8 (microbial), Eco‐Humate (organic acid) and Eco‐Vital (fish + seaweed), were applied throughout the growing season. Tomato cv. Moneymaker seedlings were transplanted into free‐draining plastic pots filled with 80:20 (v:v) field soil:river sand and inoculated with viable M. javanica eggs (~10,000/pot). At 11 weeks post‐inoculation, the roots were washed free of soil and scored for RKN‐induced galling and egg counts. Rhizosphere soil and root samples were then sequenced to identify bacterial communities. Tomato plants grown in preconditioned field soil had significant reductions in RKN galling (31.8% [microbial], 26.3% [fish + seaweed] and 25.4% [organic acid]) compared to untreated control soil. Amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene showed significant differences in bacterial community composition between the plants grown in preconditioned soil and the controls. These findings suggest that the biological products created a potential legacy effect that contributed to RKN suppression and highlight the potential of the products for integrated management of RKNs, and the need for further investigation in replicated field trials.

titel: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Activity of Isothiocyanate-Triazine Conjugates as AChE and BACE1 Inhibitors
zusammenfassung: The search for new compounds capable of inhibiting the activity of enzymes involved in the development of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease, has attracted continuing interest for many years. Natural isothiocyanates and their synthetic analogs, as well as compounds containing a 1,3,5-triazine core, constitute a group of molecules with complex mechanisms of action involving multiple molecular targets. Although literature data confirm the activity of both isothiocyanates and s-triazines, these two active fragments have not yet been combined, and it remains unclear whether a synergistic effect can be achieved. In this study, 11 novel isothiocyanate–triazine conjugates, consisting of a 1,3,5-triazine core substituted with aliphatic or cyclic secondary amines and a phosphorus analogue of isothiocyanate [6-(isothiocyanatohexyl)phosphonate)ethyl], were synthesized with yields of 46–80%. The pharmacokinetic profiles and parameters related to Lipinski’s rule of five were determined for all compounds. All compounds were evaluated as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and β-secretase (BACE1). Compound 1i showed the highest inhibitory activity against AChE (IC50 = 0.182 ± 0.02 µM), while compound 1b exhibited the strongest inhibition of BACE1 (IC50 = 8.48 ± 2.18 µM). To explore the potential of these multifunctional derivatives, plausible enzyme-ligand binding models were proposed based on molecular docking simulations.

titel: Do Drivers Incorporate Vehicle Dynamics When Estimating Time Required to Turn in a Driving Simulator?
ort: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
zusammenfassung: Safe turning decisions rely on drivers accurately estimating an oncoming vehicle’s time-to-collision and their own time-required-to-turn (TRT). A previous driving simulator experiment that investigated the accuracy of TRT judgments found that people underestimated how long it took them to turn. A potential limitation of this study is that participants may have used vehicle dynamics from a personal vehicle to estimate TRT rather than using the vehicle dynamics from the driving simulator. The current study manipulated the vehicle dynamics depicted in the driving simulator to determine if participants adjusted their TRT estimates to the vehicle they drove. Participants completed two conditions: one in which the vehicle dynamics resembled a sports car and one in which the vehicle dynamics resembled a truck. Results indicated that people adjusted their turn estimations according to the vehicle dynamics depicted in the driving simulator, and people underestimate their own TRT.

titel: Whole-Cell and Acellular Pertussis Vaccines: A Narrative Review of Biological, Clinical, Safety and Programmatic Evidence, with Implications for Poland
zusammenfassung: Background/Objectives: Pertussis has resurged worldwide despite long-standing vaccination programs. Whole-cell (wP) and acellular (aP) pertussis vaccines differ in immunobiology, durability, reactogenicity, and programmatic use. Poland is the only European Union/European Economic Area (EU/EEA) country that routinely primes infants with wP while using aP products for boosters, pregnancy, and selected indications, providing an informative programmatic context. This review compares both platforms across biological, clinical, safety, epidemiological, and supply domains. Methods: We conducted a narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE literature and documents from the World Health Organization, European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, national public health institutes, and regulatory authorities through July 2026. No protocol was registered and no quantitative synthesis was performed. Results: wP priming induces a persistent T-helper 1/T-helper 17-oriented response and an immunoglobulin G1-dominant profile, whereas aP vaccination produces higher, higher-avidity antibody concentrations, an increasing immunoglobulin G4 fraction, and substantially lower reactogenicity. Historical trials demonstrated marked product-level heterogeneity: efficacy ranged from 36–48% for poorly performing wP vaccines to 84–85% for multicomponent aP vaccines, while one United Kingdom wP product performed comparably to a five-component aP vaccine. Protection after aP schedules wanes within several years, no validated correlate of protection exists, and neither intramuscular platform reliably prevents colonization or transmission. In 2024, eight aP-using EU/EEA countries had higher pertussis notification rates than Poland despite stable Polish infant coverage. Conclusions: Neither platform is uniformly superior across products, schedules, and clinically relevant outcomes. Program performance depends primarily on timely infant vaccination, maternal vaccination, appropriate boosters, product-specific effectiveness evidence, and secure vaccine supply.

titel: Narratives of psychosis-like experiences: an exploration of trauma, attachment and how people manage
zusammenfassung: Background The trauma–psychosis relationship is well established via the dose–response hypothesis, including the connection between traumatic experiences and psychosis-like experiences (PLE). PLE are commonly associated with childhood trauma and this relationship has been found to be influenced by attachment. Secure attachment can help people manage trauma and, as psychosis can be understood as a trauma-response, secure attachment may also be protective for those with PLE.Methods This study narratively explored traumatic experiences and PLE in the general population. Nine participants, with experience of trauma/adversity and PLEs, and self-defined as “managing well” undertook a narrative interview. Narrative analysis explored how their difficult experiences were managed, through the lens of attachment.Results Common narratives included escape, endurance, overcoming and exploration. titel: Utility of aPTT in Predicting 28-day Mortality in Septic AKI Patients
zusammenfassung: Background: Sepsis is an uncontrolled inflammation leading to multiple organ dysfunction. Septic acute kidney injury (AKI) is one of the leading causes of mortality. During sepsis, coagulation cascade derangement can occur. Score systems such as Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE-II) and Sequential Organ Failure Assesment have been developed, but they are not readily available in a resource-limited setting. Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and D-dimer can be used to prognosticate 28-day mortality in septic AKI patients. Patients and Method: This longitudinal observational study was conducted from March 2023 to September 2024 at the Medicine Emergency Department of the Department of General Medicine, Government Medical College and Hospital, Chandigarh. Patients diagnosed with sepsis as per the Sepsis 3.0 definition were screened for AKI using the Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes criteria. The blood investigations were sent, namely, serum electrolytes, renal function tests, liver function tests, complete blood count and coagulation profile. The results were analysed for 28-day in-hospital mortality. The main objective of our study was to determine the relationship between coagulation parameters and all-cause mortality in septic AKI patients. Results: Out of 63 patients with septic AKI, 38 (60.3%) were males, and 25 (39.7%) were females. The findings reveal that coagulation parameters of aPTT ≥80 seconds and D-dimer ≥6400 ng/mL have performance comparable to APACHE II and, therefore, can be used to predict 28-day mortality in patients with septic AKI. Conclusion: Our study revealed that aPTT and D-dimer can be used to predict 28-day mortality in septic AKI patients.

titel: Limiting dengue transmission using a differential game approach
zusammenfassung: In this paper, a fundamental structural asymmetry in dengue fever epidemic control approaches is identified and formalized. We show that treatment and quarantine interventions must influence the sick compartment, whereas the majority of epidemic game models treat interventions as affecting the susceptible compartment (e.g., vaccination). A fundamental imbalance is produced by this structural difference: public health interventions (downstream) alter the linear elimination term, whereas behavioral control (upstream) alters the bi linear incidence term. We demonstrate through careful mathematical analysis that behavioral control has a greater global impact through multiplicative effects over time, while public health measures dominate in local immediate sensitivity. For a differential game model, we calculate the open-loop Nash equilibrium and demonstrate an 86.4% decrease in peak infections when compared to no control. Our findings show that where control enters the epidemic system is just as important as how much control is applied, resolving the apparent dichotomy between local sensitivity and global impact. The best dengue management methods are significantly impacted by this structural asymmetry.

titel: Impact of photovoltaic intelligent maximum power point tracking battery charger for 50-kWh electric vehicle lithium-ion battery on carbon dioxide emissions in United Arab Emirates
zusammenfassung: Abstract Electric vehicles (EVs) represent an effective solution for reducing carbon dioxide emissions, provided their lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are charged by using clean energy and a reliance on traditional fossil-fuel-based electricity generation is avoided. This directly impacts grid performance and overall sustainability. Considering this reality, this study proposes an efficient solution for intelligent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) based on an artificial neural network (ANN) algorithm and the charging of EV batteries using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy through distributed PV systems covering both nearby and remote areas. A clean PV unit of 50 kW is proposed to reduce CO2 emissions by ∼3.7 tons annually compared with conventional fossil-fuel-based power stations by shifting to a clean solution that significantly reduces the negative impact of carbon dioxide emissions. The proposed system focuses on controlling the charging of EV batteries through continuous monitoring of the state of charge and terminal voltage of the LIB to protect the EV battery against overcharging or fully discharging. This design ensures fast and accurate MPPT performance while significantly reducing CO2 emissions. MATLAB®/Simulink® simulation results show promising indicators for an efficient battery charger for EV LIB applications. The simulation results show an efficient ANN algorithm with a low mean squared error of 0.00045023 at epoch 12, a suitable charging current ranging from 20 and 29 A, and a daily charging energy range of 40–60 kWh.

titel: Development of a Visibility Inspection System for 3D Railway Scene Using Onboard Multi‐View Camera Images
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT In railway infrastructure maintenance, rising upkeep cost by a declining labor force have become a critical challenge. Visibility inspections of obstruction warning signals—which require verification from distances of up to 800 m—are highly labor‐intensive, often performed at night and involving long walking distances. This paper proposes a novel visibility inspection system based on a 3D railway environment reconstructed from multi‐view images captured by onboard cameras. The system generates a 3D point cloud using Structure from Motion (SfM) and constructs a photorealistic environment using 3D Gaussian Splatting enabling efficient and realistic rendering of complex railway scenes. Virtual viewpoints within the reconstructed space allow accurate remote visibility inspection. Furthermore, an integrated AI model enables automatic detection and evaluation of signal visibility without human intervention. Field tests demonstrate sufficient geometric accuracy and practical applicability. The proposed system reduces labor and operational costs while maintaining high inspection quality and supports the development of automated and scalable railway maintenance strategies.

titel: Impact of E‐Cigarette Exposure on Wound Healing After Surgical Vocal Fold Injury in Mice
zusammenfassung: OBJECTIVES: Surgical manipulation of the vocal folds carries a risk of mucosal injury. titel: Bounded justice for tribal creatures: a fact-sensitive defence of patriotism
zusammenfassung: We defend patriotism against the moral arbitrariness objection. Our argument appeals to a fact-sensitive view of justice which integrates fundamental facts about the human condition into our normative theorising. We argue that tribalism, the innate tendency to favour the in-group, is a circumstance of justice and that fact-sensitive views of justice must account for it. We then present a two-step comparative argument. Practically, patriotism is a far better fit for tribalism than cosmopolitanism and other broader loyalties. Finally, compared to viable alternative loyalties, patriotism reveals robust ethical credentials: it can overcome the politics of difference while also ennobling and taming tribalism.

titel: A narrative review of qualitative studies exploring the normalization of gambling for youth and younger adults
zusammenfassung: Gambling is a highly visible and socially embedded activity among young people, with marketing, social practices, and digital platforms shaping perceptions and behaviours. This article presents a narrative review of qualitative studies (2015-25) exploring how gambling is normalized among youth and younger adults (up to 35 years), and how they perceive and respond to these processes. Four themes were constructed from n = 22 articles using a reflexive approach to thematic analysis. First, gambling was socially constructed as a normative activity through early family exposure and peer group practices, where participation could both encourage and discourage engagement. Second, exposure to gambling advertising, particularly through sport, was a pervasive driver of normalization, framing gambling as entertaining, glamorous, and overwhelmingly positive. titel: Searching for the truth? search engines and their AI affordances’ responses to conspiratorial search practices
zusammenfassung: Search engines are a common pathway to conspiracy theories, and producers of conspiratorial narratives actively encourage users to search for particular terms. zusammenfassung: The development of the first cardiac troponin T assay (cTnT) in 1987 was a major breakthrough in the clinical diagnosis of myocardial infarction (1). The fifth-generation cTnT assay (Elecsys® Troponin T hs, Roche Diagnostics) was the first cardiac troponin assay to meet the definition of a high-sensitivity (hs) assay by achieving a CV ≤ 10% at the 99th percentile of a healthy reference population and being able to measure cardiac troponin above the limit of detection (LoD) in at least 50% of healthy individuals (2). Greater analytical sensitivity has enabled more precise determination of the upper reference limit (URL) (3). Accelerated diagnostic pathways have harnessed this by incorporating risk stratification thresholds below the URL that enable the diagnosis of myocardial infarction to be excluded at presentation (4). Implementation of these pathways has reduced unnecessary hospital admissions, serial testing, and length of stay (5, 6), and these pathways are now widely recommended by clinical practice guidelines (7). While the fifth-generation hs-cTnT assay is the most widely used cardiac troponin assay worldwide, some limitations have impacted its performance in clinical practice. First, interference from sample haemolysis and biotin can falsely lower reported cTnT concentrations and may lead to sample rejection and delays in the diagnosis (8). Second, chronic elevations in cTnT without acute myocardial injury are common in clinical practice (9). The optimal approach to investigate these patients further is uncertain. Third, most accelerated diagnostic pathways have used the LoD of this assay to identify low-risk patients at presentation, but in the United States, the assay is not FDA-cleared to report concentrations below the limit of quantitation (LoQ), resulting in some variation in adoption. Finally, reference range studies performed using different enrollment criteria in Europe and the United States have resulted in divergence in the manufacturer-recommended URLs and some uncertainty about the value of sex-specific URLs. In 2025, the manufacturer released the sixth generation of this assay (Elecsys® Troponin T hs Gen 6, Roche Diagnostics), which is CE-marked and aims to offer greater analytical precision at low concentrations and resistance to interference. In a large, international reference range study, the new assay demonstrated that cTnT concentrations differ by sex across the normal range, with 99th percentile URLs that are 2-fold lower in females (18 ng/L) compared with males (32 ng/L) (10). The assay targets the same cTnT epitopes as the fifth-generation assay, using a matured capture antibody with increased affinity. However, the sixth-generation assay is now standardized against traceable reference materials prepared with recombinant human, rather than bovine, cTnT, which was used for previous iterations. Importantly, as a consequence of this change in standardization materials, the fifth- and sixth-generation hs-cTnT assays do not yield equivalent results. In this issue, Ge et al. and Knoll et al. report findings from 2 studies that have evaluated the analytical performance of the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay. Both investigating teams followed CLSI protocols to evaluate the precision, repeatability, calibration, and resistance to interference (11, 12). Ge et al. evaluated the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay using the Roche cobas e 801 analyzer in a clinical laboratory using recombinant cTnT spiked into plasma samples to create known target concentrations. The limit of blank and LoD were measured using duplicate tests of analyte-free and low cTnT samples over 3 days, while the LoQ was determined by testing low samples daily over 20 days. The limit of blank, LoD, and LoQ were found to be lower than the fifth-generation assay, and linearity was maintained at high values. Precision of the assay was assessed across multiple quality control and plasma samples, resulting in a CV below 10% for repeatability (within a single run), as well as for intermediate precision (within one laboratory) across the range of cardiac troponin T values. Both skeletal troponin T and purified cardiac troponin I/C isoforms were spiked into the plasma samples, and minimal cross-reactivity was observed using the sixth-generation assay. Interference from hemolysis was undetectable up to concentrations of 5000 mg/dL of hemoglobin, which may reduce the need for clinical laboratories to request repeat blood samples (11). Similarly, Knoll et al. evaluated the analytical performance of the sixth-generation assay across 3 analysers (Roche Cobas® e 801 and e 402 and Pro analyzers) and 4 reagent lots, using both serum and lithium–heparin plasma samples obtained from biobanks. Repeated analysis of duplicates, including analyte-free and low cTnT samples, was also conducted. Similarly, the sixth-generation assay was found to have high analytical precision, and was able to detect cardiac troponin T in 90% of samples that fell below the LoD of the fifth-generation assay. The limit of blank and LoQ were low and met prespecified targets. Linearity was shown across the range of measured values and maintained across all analysers and reagent lots. Complementing the study findings by Ge et al., the CV was below 10% for repeatability and intermediate precision using multiple quality control and native cTnT samples across 3 reagent lots. The assay was resistant to interference from hemolysis up to a threshold of 1000 mg/dL—10 times the tolerance of the previous assay—and interference from biotin, bilirubin, and antistreptavidin antibodies was also reduced (12). The consistency of the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay across multiple analysers and reagent lots is an important analytical attribute, providing confidence that the assay will perform comparably over time and in different laboratories. The authors did not observe any systematic difference in sixth-generation hs-cTnT measurements between samples from serum and heparinized plasma matrices (12). However, Ge et al. observed a negative bias of 11% when measuring in citrate plasma samples (11). For clinicians, it will be important to know whether these changes in analytical performance, assay standardization, and URLs will impact the clinical performance of the hs-cTnT assay. Three recently published observational cohort studies of patients with possible myocardial infarction provide complementary insights (13–15). The proportion of patients with myocardial injury (defined as any cTnT concentration above the sex-specific URL) was lower for the sixth-generation compared to the fifth-generation hs-cTnT assay in Thurston et al. (22% vs 27%), Völschow et al. (38% vs 41%), and Koechlin et al. (36% vs 44%). All 3 studies found that discrimination for myocardial infarction was similar for both assays. Greater precision of the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay at low concentrations may improve the effectiveness of risk-stratification thresholds applied in single-sample rule-out pathways. For the fifth-generation hs-cTnT assay, analytical imprecision at low concentrations precluded optimization of this threshold, and therefore, the LoD or LoQ was applied. However, the gain in precision with the sixth-generation assay will enable the use of thresholds defined based on clinical performance rather than analytical imprecision, which may increase the proportion of patients identified as low risk at presentation and reduce the need for serial testing (13–15). The need for fewer repeat blood draws due to hemolysis, improved reliability of performance across sample matrices and analytical platforms, identification of more low-risk patients at presentation, and a reduction in the proportion of patients with myocardial injury while maintaining sensitivity for myocardial infarction are all attractive features of the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay. Whether these improvements in the assay will result in cTnT becoming a better cardiac biomarker requires further study. Prospective studies reporting the impact of implementing the sixth-generation assay will determine whether greater analytical performance translates into clinical benefits in the real world. What will the impact be on hospital admissions, length of stay, and the need for serial measurements? Will the identification of fewer patients with myocardial injury have implications for patient care and safety? Will the sixth-generation assay be more cost-effective than the fifth-generation assay and impact resource allocation? Could greater precision at low concentrations lead to new roles for risk stratification in the outpatient setting? Given how widely the current hs-cTnT assay is used around the world, addressing these questions is a priority to fully understand the impact on patient care of adopting the sixth-generation hs-cTnT assay. titel: The Leadership Premium: Committee Leadership Status and Political Donations to Incumbent Legislators in South Korea
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effect of committee leadership positions on political fundraising in the South Korean National Assembly from 2004 to 2019. Drawing upon theories of legislative power and campaign finance, we examine whether acquiring standing committee chairmanships significantly increases political contributions received by legislators, even within Korea's highly restrictive regulatory regime that prohibits corporate donations. Utilizing OLS regression and difference‐in‐differences with Panel Matching methodology, we find compelling evidence of a substantial leadership premium. OLS estimates reveal that committee chairs consistently outraise non‐chairs by 16%–21%; Panel Matching estimates confirm an immediate increase of approximately 1.15 log‐points (a 216% increase) following chair appointment. Event study analysis validates our identification strategy by demonstrating parallel pre‐trends and sharp treatment effects at the moment of leadership transition, with effects dissipating after chairs leave their positions. Split‐sample OLS estimates reveal a cross‐over pattern: the premium is significant for Targeted and Mixed committees in the first half of the legislative term but shifts to Universal committees in the second half, suggesting that the relevant dimension of heterogeneity may be whether a committee holds jurisdictional authority over concentrated regulatory or budgetary stakes. These findings demonstrate that the link between institutional power and political money persists even under highly restrictive campaign finance regimes—reflecting structural features of legislative organization that transcend specific regulatory designs. The individual‐as‐proxy mechanism we identify, whereby organized interest groups circumvent the corporate donation ban through coordinated individual‐level contributions, suggests that regulation reshapes the channels of strategic giving without eliminating its underlying demand.

titel: Correlation of right heart catheterization and duplex ultrasound to identify fistula volume flow
zusammenfassung: OBJECTIVES: Arteriovenous fistula is the preferred form of hemodialysis access. Positive remodeling may result in high flow vascular access (HFVA), leading to elevated right heart pressures, cardiomyopathy and in advanced presentation-high-output heart failure (HOHF). Noninvasive duplex ultrasound (DUS) is the most commonly accepted mode of surveillance for HFVA. The reliability of DUS compared to the gold standard modality of right heart catheterization (RHC) to quantify access circuit volume flow (Qa) has not been reported. Our aim is to analyze a cohort of patients with suspected HOHF who underwent both studies and evaluate the concordance between Qa measurements. METHODS: We identified a consecutive cohort of eight patients with suspected HFVA and HOHF requiring diagnostic RHC. Qa was calculated by DUS and RHC. The association between the two measures was calculated using Pearson correlation, and agreement was assessed with Lin's concordance correlation coefficient. We evaluate the association between brachial artery (BA) diameter and the Qa agreement. RESULTS: The mean Qa measured by DUS was 2623 ml/min, compared to a mean of 1538 ml/min measured by RHC. On average, the Qa measured by the DUS was 1086 ml/min greater than the RHC measurement, representing a 104% incremental difference. Only two of the eight cases (25%) had Qa measures within 500 ml/min. This discordance was greatest with a larger BA diameter, where a lower agreement measure of 0.39 and a moderate range correlation of 0.55 was found between Qa measured with RHC and DUS. CONCLUSION: Although DUS is the most utilized modality to monitor Qa, low correlation is observed compared to RHC, discrepancy that is directly associated with BA diameter and may reflect true overestimation of Qa by DUS or result from measurements obtained under differing hemodynamic conditions (e.g. heart rate variability). RHC should be used more liberally for the diagnosis and management of HFVA, particularly when HOHF is suspected.

titel: Consensus on prevention and management of thrombosis related to temporary nontunneled central venous catheters in hemodialysis
zusammenfassung: Nontunneled central venous catheters (CVCs) are widely used for urgent and short-term vascular access in blood purification therapy, but catheter-related thrombosis remains a frequent and clinically important complication. It may cause catheter dysfunction, treatment interruption, premature catheter removal, additional interventions, pulmonary embolism, and increased mortality risk. This consensus summarizes current evidence on the epidemiology, classification, risk factors, prevention, evaluation, and management of thrombosis associated with nontunneled CVCs in blood purification therapy. Key preventive strategies include appropriate catheter indications, minimized dwell time, preference for the right internal jugular vein, ultrasound-guided insertion, standardized catheter care, and appropriate locking solutions. Evaluation should combine clinical recognition with stepwise imaging, with color Doppler ultrasonography as the first-line modality. Management should be individualized according to thrombus location and severity, including thrombolysis, anticoagulation, catheter removal, and selective interventional or surgical treatment.

titel: Whole-of-system approach for program implementation: Lessons from the Australian Teletrial Program
zusammenfassung: Decentralized clinical trial (DCT) methods have evolved globally to improve access to clinical trials for rural, regional, and other underserved populations. Several countries, including Australia, have implemented DCT approaches with variable success.In Australia, the Australian Teletrial Model was developed and adopted as a national policy initiative to improve equitable access to clinical trials. The Australian Teletrial Program, funded by the Commonwealth Government, supported implementation across jurisdictions and health services.The program achieved several important outcomes, including the development of harmonized templates and processes, standard operating procedures, and education and training programs. It also improved patient access to trials and strengthened workforce capability across participating sites.Despite these achievements, several barriers continue to limit broader implementation and sustainability. These include workforce turnover, cumbersome approval processes, variable uptake across different levels of the health system and sponsors, and inconsistent leadership engagement and ownership. Such challenges have constrained scale and productivity.To fully realize the benefits of DCT models and support health equity objectives, a whole-of-system approach is required. Streamlined policies and processes, aligned governance, and sustained leadership commitment are needed to embed decentralized clinical trial models into routine healthcare delivery and ensure long-term sustainability, productivity, and equitable access to clinical research.

titel: Single-cell RNA sequencing in diabetic foot ulcers: pathogenesis, biomarkers, and translational potential
ort: Frontiers in Clinical Diabetes and Healthcare
zusammenfassung: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU), a common diabetic complication driven by impaired angiogenesis, neuropathy and metabolic disorders, has complex pathogenesis and poses great challenges to clinical management. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), an emerging transcriptomic technique, allows disease profiling at single-cell resolution. This review summarizes recent advances in scRNA-seq-based DFU research, revealing that JMJD3-mediated macrophage polarization failure and dysregulated IGF-1-SP1-CD248 pathway hinder wound repair, with MMP1, MMP3, MMP11 , JMJD3 and HIF1A identified as valuable biomarkers and therapeutic targets. titel: Group Cable Bolt Interaction and Preliminary Spacing Assessment in Deep Stopes Based on a Dual-Index Interaction Framework
zusammenfassung: Spacing design for group cable bolt systems remains largely empirical and rarely considers stress interaction and displacement overlap together. This study develops a dual-index interaction framework for two representative cable bolt configurations in deep stope roofs. Mindlin’s semi-infinite body solution and Kelvin’s infinite body solution were combined with a non-uniform interfacial shear stress distribution to model shallow fully grouted and deep end-anchored systems, respectively. The analytical trends were examined using FLAC3D, and the field applicability of the selected spacing scheme was assessed through an industrial test at the Fankou Lead–Zinc Mine. The results show that the fully grouted configuration is strongly affected by the free surface and full-length load transfer, whereas interaction in the end-anchored configuration is concentrated around the deep bonded section. The stress interaction coefficient η provides the primary screening measure for a reference lower spacing bound, while the displacement interaction coefficient α identifies residual displacement overlap. Both are local field interaction indices rather than measures of individual cable capacity or global system stiffness. Using ηref = 0.9 as an engineering tolerance, stress interaction becomes limited at approximately s/D = 30 for the end-anchored configuration, whereas the fully grouted configuration enters a relatively stable interaction–attenuation stage at approximately s/D = 40. Considering both configurations, s/D ≈ 40 is adopted as a reference lower bound, corresponding to 1.6 m for a 40 mm borehole. The field scheme used a spacing of 1.8 m (s/D ≈ 45) and produced a maximum measured roof displacement of 27.6 mm, with no evident roof fall, cable breakage, or anchorage pull-out. Because characteristic rock mass heterogeneity is not explicitly represented and only one field spacing was tested, the proposed spacing ratio should be regarded as condition-specific rather than universal.

titel: Research on climate effects of large herbivores in Europe: a systematic map
zusammenfassung: Abstract Background Land management practices have significant impacts on biodiversity and climate change processes. Conservation and rewilding practitioners are increasingly seeking to enhance ecosystem functions and carbon sequestration simultaneously, encouraged by climate policies such as the European Green Deal. In recent years, ecosystem restoration involving large herbivores (≥ 10 kg) has attracted growing interest. However, the climate impacts of large herbivores are complex, including direct and indirect impacts from greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, carbon storage, wildfire and albedo. These impacts can have cooling or warming effects and vary with species, herd density, season and habitat. To date, the diverse research on this topic has not been collated and categorised in a systematic map. Here, we present a systematic map of research on the climate effects of large herbivores in European terrestrial habitats, highlighting research distribution, clusters and gaps, and the potential for further quantitative analyses. We address the primary question of what research exists on the climate effects of large herbivores in Europe. Methods Following our pre-published protocol, we used a pre-defined search string to conduct a search of peer-reviewed and grey literature, using a range of bibliographic databases, search engines and websites. We screened search results for relevance in two stages: by title and abstract, then full text. We excluded articles that failed to meet the eligibility criteria of terrestrial habitats in Europe (Population), large herbivores (Exposure) and climate impacts (Outcome). We coded the included studies by multiple variables, recorded in a spreadsheet alongside the narrative synthesis. Review findings We identified 316 articles for inclusion, involving a total of 565 studies (different research comparisons within the same article). Most studies were conducted in Northern Europe (63%), with the largest research cluster in the United Kingdom. Eastern Europe had the fewest studies (6%). The most frequently studied large herbivores were cattle (included in 54% of studies), sheep (34%) and reindeer (7%). Other types of large herbivores were included in fewer than 5% of studies (these included goats, equines, various species of wild cervids, European bison, pigs, wild boars, goat-antelopes (chamois), water buffaloes, beavers, and tortoises). The most frequently studied climate-related outcomes were soil carbon (included in 34% of studies), nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions (33%), carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) flux or emissions (21%) and enteric methane (CH 4 ) emissions (17%). Few studies combined multiple climate-related effects to estimate net emissions (6%). Conclusions The systematic map demonstrates substantial research gaps on the climate impacts of large herbivores. Research has predominantly focused on large domestic herbivores in agricultural contexts, particularly cattle and sheep. The research gaps for other large herbivores (and for natural and semi-natural habitats) present difficulties for conservation and rewilding practitioners in assessing the climate implications of their choices regarding large herbivores used in land management. The paucity of studies addressing net GHG emissions (accounting for multiple GHGs and carbon sequestration) also present challenges for determining which choices are likely to have net climate benefits. These research gaps have implications for policy and practice, particularly for nature-based carbon offsetting projects. Research to address these gaps would aid decision-making in both nature recovery and climate change mitigation.

titel: Motivational and emotional determinants of health goal progress in inflammatory bowel disease: a longitudinal study
zusammenfassung: Background: Self-management among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is influenced by motivational and emotional factors. Although research has increasingly highlighted psychological support, it has underexplored interactions among goal-related emotions, motivation types, and progress in health-related behavior. Methods: A total of 123 adults diagnosed with IBD participated in a longitudinal study, completing questionnaires at baseline (T1) and at follow-ups after three months (T2) and six months (T3). Measures included self-concordance (autonomous and controlled motivation), positive and negative emotions, and goal progress. Longitudinal relations were assessed using a two-step latent-score approach and structural equation modeling. Results: Autonomous motivation at T1 and T2 predicted more positive emotions at T2 and T3. Positive emotions at T2, in turn, predicted greater autonomous motivation at T3. Controlled motivation at T1 predicted more negative emotions at T2. Additionally, positive emotions at T1 predicted better goal progress at T2, which further increased positive emotions at T3. Conclusions: The findings identified reciprocal, mutually reinforcing associations between autonomous motivation and positive emotions, as well as between positive emotions and perceived progress toward health-related goals. Supporting these self-reinforcing processes may strengthen the long-term self-regulation required for effective self-management in individuals living with IBD.

titel: Compensatory yield responses drive high performance of soybeans treated with seed-applied Soyfx®: an on-farm experimental study

titel: Organ Size and Metabolic Rate Co‐Vary with Dimensions of the Obstetric Pelvis: The Metabolic Coordination of Childbirth Hypothesis
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT Objectives Childbirth complications occur if fetal size is excessive for the maternal birth canal. Associations between metabolic and pelvic traits were assessed using Pearson correlations, and partial correlations adjusting for height or tibia length. Fat mass was associated with REE and organ/muscle mass but not pelvic dimensions. titel: Multi-Sensor Downscaling of Land Surface Temperature Using Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 Imagery: Evidence from Dhaka City, Bangladesh
zusammenfassung: Rapid urbanization and increasing land surface temperatures (LSTs) have intensified urban heat stress in rapidly growing tropical megacities such as Dhaka. However, the coarse spatial resolution of conventional thermal satellite imagery limits the identification of fine-scale urban thermal variability required for climate-sensitive urban planning. This study develops a multi-sensor LST downscaling framework by integrating Landsat 8 thermal imagery with Sentinel-2-derived spectral indices within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform. A random forest regression model was developed using the normalized difference vegetation index, normalized difference built-up index, and modified normalized difference water index as predictors for statistical downscaling from the 30 m Landsat grid to a nominal 10 m grid. To preserve localized thermal heterogeneity and improve radiometric consistency, a bicubic residual correction approach was incorporated into the downscaling workflow. The resulting statistically downscaled LST estimate on a nominal 10 m grid was subsequently used to classify Urban Thermal Zones (UTZs) across Dhaka City. The results showed that LST was negatively associated with vegetation and water-related indices and positively associated with the built-up index. The statistically downscaled product provided a more spatially detailed representation of the Landsat-derived thermal field and delineated relative surface-temperature hotspots and cooler zones across the study area. High-temperature zones were primarily concentrated within densely built-up commercial and industrial areas, whereas comparatively lower temperatures were observed in vegetated and water-dominated regions. The proposed framework demonstrates a computationally efficient approach to spatially refining Landsat-derived LST in a data-constrained tropical megacity. The findings provide valuable spatial information for urban climate adaptation, heat mitigation planning, and climate-resilient urban development.

titel: Baseline and 72-h dynamic laboratory deficit burden for mortality through day 90 after acute ischemic stroke in critical care: landmark analyses with temporal validation
zusammenfassung: Background A laboratory-based frailty index (FI-Lab) summarizes routinely measured deficits, but during critical illness it may reflect acute derangement and underlying vulnerability. The 24-h cohort comprised patients alive with evaluable 0–24 h FI-Lab; the 72-h cohort comprised those alive with evaluable baseline and 24–72 h FI-Lab. Each outcome was death after the applicable landmark through day 90 after ICU admission. Clinical logistic models were compared with models incorporating baseline FI-Lab, change direction, a four-level phenotype, or continuous baseline and change. We assessed discrimination, calibration, decision curves, and paired bootstrap differences, with sensitivity analyses defined for the revised analysis. zusammenfassung: Starch modification through physical processing represents a promising "green" strategy to enhance food functionality and nutritional quality while meeting clean-label demands. This review offers a critical overview of the structural and nutritional impacts of physical modifications coupled with an exploratory use of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted literature for screening and mining. Focused on literature published between 2001 and 2026, a traditional human-led systematic search identifies eligible studies that examined the effects of three major commercially relevant modification techniques-annealing (ANN), heat-moisture treatment (HMT), and autoclaving-on rapidly digestible starch (RDS), slowly digestible starch (SDS), and resistant starch (RS), with emphasis on resistant starch type III (RS3). Among the evaluated techniques, autoclaving, particularly when followed by retrogradation, appears to offer the greatest potential for increasing RS relative to the original native starch. However, its effectiveness is strongly dependent on the raw material, with substantial gains arising from its amylose content, while waxy starches may show little improvement or even a reduction in RS. ANN tends to produce milder and more variable effects, often shifting starch from RDS toward SDS. HMT generally reduces RDS and increases SDS, making it a promising approach for attenuating glycemic responses. However, the extent of these changes can vary substantially depending on the starch source, amylose content, moisture level, and processing temperature. Overall, the work revisits the potential of physical processing as an avenue for starch engineering while underlining a pressing need for standardized workflows, harmonized methodologies, and unified protocols for quantification of starch digestibility, namely, of RS levels. Lastly, the review exemplifies AI can accelerate preliminary literature identification and synthesis yet highlights gaps in AI aptitudes for independent quantitative integration that still maintains a need for thorough human-driven validation.

titel: A study on the effects of CCRT on cognitive function and blood biomarkers in community-dwelling older adults with MCI
zusammenfassung: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of Computerized Cognitive Remediation Therapy (CCRT) on cognitive function and blood biomarker levels in community-dwelling older adults with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and to provide objective evidence for evaluating the effectiveness of CCRT. METHODS: This randomized controlled trial included 68 participants who completed the intervention and were included in the final analysis (37 in the intervention group and 31 in the control group). The control group received health education, while the intervention group received both health education and a 12-week CCRT intervention. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) before and after the intervention. Plasma levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and phosphorylated Tau181 (P-tau181) were also measured at baseline and post-intervention. Linear mixed-effects models and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to examine the effects of CCRT on cognitive function and biomarker levels, as well as the predictive value of biomarkers for cognitive improvement. RESULTS: After the 12-week intervention, the intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in MMSE and MoCA total scores compared to the control group (MMSE: P = 0.007; MoCA: P = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed in memory (MMSE: P = 0.027), language (MMSE: P = 0.018; MoCA: P < 0.001), and attention (MoCA: P < 0.001). Plasma GFAP levels significantly decreased in the intervention group compared to the control group (P < 0.001), while no significant difference was found in P-tau181 levels (P = 0.501). ROC curve analysis showed that a reduction in GFAP levels significantly predicted cognitive improvement in MCI patients (AUC = 0.805, P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that a 12-week CCRT intervention can significantly improve cognitive function and reduce GFAP levels in community-dwelling older adults with MCI. The change in GFAP is associated with cognitive improvement, suggesting its potential as an objective biomarker for evaluating intervention effectiveness. titel: Relationship of Adult Cervical Spinous Processes to Vertebral Midline for Cervical Disc Replacement
zusammenfassung: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort.ObjectivesAccurate, midline artificial disc placement is crucial when performing cervical disc replacement (CDR). Although cervical spinous processes (SPs) are considered midline structures, clinical experience has often shown noticeable deviation at times. This study aims to quantitatively characterize this known observation to better understand the utility of SPs as midline indicators during CDR.MethodsPatients who underwent anterior cervical discectomy and fusion with preoperative cervical spine computerized tomography (CT) scans were retrospectively identified, excluding those with previously surgically altered spines. Angular and lateral SP deviations from C3-C7 were collected from these CTs. Statistical analysis was conducted using one-way ANOVA with post-hoc testing using Tukey's test.ResultsThe average angular SP deviations at C3-C7 were 2.94 ± 2.06 degrees, 3.52 ± 2.19 degrees, 3.50 ± 2.13 degrees, 4.31 ± 2.15 degrees, and 3.53 ± 2.86 degrees, respectively. The average lateral SP deviations at C3-C7 relative to vertebral body widths were 5.43%, 6.10%, 6.14%, 8.17%, and 7.52%, respectively. Angular deviation at C6 was greater than C3 (p = 0.009). Relative lateral deviation at C6 was greater than at C3 (p = 0.027). Neither angular nor lateral deviation differed by sex at any level (p > 0.05 for all).ConclusionsGiven significant variation in cervical SP deviation between patients and by level, surgeons should hesitate to solely rely on them for determining vertebral midline during CDR. The C6 and C7 SPs especially should be used cautiously as they show relatively higher magnitudes and variations of deviation. titel: Short‐Term Nociceptive Memory: Reduced Discriminability and Multiple Encoding Biases
zusammenfassung: BACKGROUND: Distortions in pain memory carry important clinical implications, yet the processes underlying retention of nociceptive information remain incompletely understood. This study examined how the intensity of painful somatosensory inputs is maintained in memory over different intervals. METHODS: Twenty-five participants received pairs of nociceptive or non-nociceptive electrical stimuli at varying inter-stimulus intervals (3, 8, 13, 18 s), and judged whether the second stimulus was of higher, equal, or lower intensity than the first. RESULTS: In accordance with Weber-Fletcher Law, perceptual discriminability was lower in the nociceptive condition, leading to a decreased accuracy despite comparable confidence ratings. Memory performance declined with temporal delay similarly for both modalities. Accuracy increased when the second stimulus was more intense than the first. For nociceptive stimuli only, accuracy deteriorated disproportionately when the second stimulus was weaker, suggesting a directional encoding bias specific to pain. When errors occurred, participants overestimated the intensity of the second stimulus, a bias more pronounced for nociceptive stimuli. Such overestimation was linked to memory encoding and disappeared when participants rated stimuli without memory demand. CONCLUSIONS: Short-term memory for nociceptive stimuli proved less accurate, more directionally biased, and more prone to overestimation than for non-nociceptive inputs. While this performance gap is largely explained by reduced perceptual discriminability at pain intensities, modality-specific distortions point to additional constraints imposed by nociceptive processing on memory encoding and maintenance. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides psychophysical evidence for differences in short-term memory retention of nociceptive versus non-nociceptive sensory input, with implications for understanding pain memory distortions in clinical contexts.

titel: Relationship Between Cyberbullying and Social Anxiety, School Refusal, and Academic Goals in Adolescents
zusammenfassung: Examining the associations between cyberbullying involvement and psychoeducational factors may contribute to a better understanding of adolescents’ experiences in online peer contexts. The findings showed that the associations varied according to both the psychoeducational dimension and the cyberbullying role. Learning and Achievement goals were negatively associated with cybervictimization, cyberaggression, and cyberbystanding, whereas Social reinforcement goals were positively associated with cyberaggression. These findings highlight the multidimensional nature of the associations between psychoeducational factors and cyberbullying involvement and support the consideration of individual and educational variables in the design of prevention and intervention strategies during adolescence.

titel: Editorial: Harnessing digital innovation for sustainable agricultural development, part II: digital transformation, agribusiness systems, and the future of food value chains
zusammenfassung: Methodologically, the Research Topic is characterised primarily by quantitative empirical analyses using cross-sectional surveys, provincial panel datasets and quasi-natural experiments, complemented by simulation-based approaches such as agent-based modelling and evolutionary game theory. These approaches provide important evidence on associations, strategic interactions and system behaviour, although they are generally less suited to examining long-term institutional change or causal pathways over extended periods Several studies converge on the importance of digital technologies for improving supply chain resilience and operational efficiency. Ding et al. (2025) demonstrate that the digital economy strengthens resilience within China's food supply chains through improved information integration and adaptive capacity. Similarly, Zhang et al. (2025a) show that digital transformation enhances transportation synergy resilience, while Zhou et al. (2025) identify digital financial risk management as a critical determinant of efficient agricultural supply chain financing. Collectively, these studies suggest that resilience is increasingly driven by the ability of firms and institutions to exchange timely, accurate, and actionable information across interconnected networks. This convergence supports a systems perspective in which resilience emerges from coordination among multiple actors rather than from improvements at individual firms.The collection also provides complementary evidence regarding digital transformation at the enterprise level. Rong et al. (2025) explain digital transformation as a strategic process influenced by interactions among firms, governments, and markets, whereas Yuan et al. (2025) demonstrate that digital transformation directly enhances agribusiness performance and long-term sustainability. Wang and Jia (2025) extend this discussion by showing that economic policy uncertainty can either stimulate or constrain enterprise digitalization depending on firms' risk management strategies. When considered together, these studies indicate that successful digital transformation depends not only on technological investments but also on supportive institutional environments, adaptive organizational capabilities, and coherent public policies. The implication is that technology alone is insufficient to drive transformation; complementary investments in governance, managerial capacity, and institutional learning are equally important.Another important theme emerging across the studies concerns transparency and trust within food value chains. Bai et al. (2025) illustrate how combining generative artificial intelligence with blockchain technology can improve coordination and product quality assurance through intelligent decision support and decentralized verification systems. Similarly, Zhang et al. (2025b) propose blockchain adoption strategies that optimize supply chain cost-sharing arrangements, while Li et al. (2025) demonstrate that consumer acceptance of blockchain traceability depends on both technological perceptions and trust-related factors. These predominantly China-based studies collectively suggest that blockchain technologies create value not merely through improved traceability but by reducing information asymmetries that have historically undermined confidence among producers, processors, retailers, and consumers. This represents an important conceptual shift from viewing blockchain as a technical innovation to understanding it as an institutional mechanism for strengthening governance within agricultural value chains.The studies further illustrate that digital transformation is increasingly shaping agricultural markets and consumer behaviour. Li and Ji (2025) show how digital information and emotional contagion influence food price dynamics during animal disease outbreaks, highlighting the growing influence of online information ecosystems on agricultural markets. Pan et al. (2025), in contrast, focus on international competitiveness and demonstrate that digital transformation contributes to market expansion by improving competitiveness within global value chains. Together, these contributions reveal that digitalization simultaneously affects both the supply side and demand side of agricultural markets through enhanced information exchange, market transparency, and consumer engagement. Despite these complementary findings, the Research Topic also reveals several important gaps that present opportunities for future investigation. First, the overwhelming majority of studies are situated within the Chinese context. While China provides an important laboratory for studying digital agriculture because of its substantial investments in digital infrastructure and rural revitalization, questions remain regarding the transferability of these findings to other developing regions where institutional environments, infrastructure quality, market structures, and digital readiness differ considerably. Expanding comparative international research would strengthen understanding of context-specific and universally applicable drivers of digital transformation.Second, most studies employ cross-sectional data, provincial panel datasets, quasinatural experiments, or simulation approaches that primarily capture short-to mediumterm impacts. Although these methodologies provide robust evidence regarding associations between digitalization and agricultural outcomes, relatively little is known about the long-term sustainability of digital transformation processes. Questions remain regarding technology adoption trajectories, organizational learning, technological obsolescence, and the persistence of digital benefits over time. Longitudinal research following firms, supply chains, and farming communities through different stages of digital maturity would substantially enrich current knowledge. Third, while technological innovations receive considerable attention, relatively fewer studies investigate the institutional and behavioural dimensions of digital transformation. Successful digitalization depends on trust, governance arrangements, organizational culture, digital leadership, regulatory frameworks, and stakeholder collaboration. Yet these factors remain underexplored compared with analyses of technological efficiency or economic performance. Future research would benefit from integrating insights from institutional economics, innovation systems theory, organizational behaviour, and public policy to better explain why similar technologies generate different outcomes across regions and organizations.Another notable gap concerns inclusiveness within digital food systems. Most studies implicitly assume that digital transformation benefits supply chains and agribusinesses as a whole. However, relatively limited attention is paid to whether these benefits are distributed equitably among smallholders, women, youth, informal enterprises, and marginalized communities. As digital technologies increasingly become prerequisites for market participation, future research should examine whether digital transformation inadvertently reinforces existing inequalities through unequal access to infrastructure, finance, digital skills, or data ownership. Addressing issues of digital inclusion will be essential if technological progress is to contribute meaningfully to the Sustainable Development Goals.The collection also points toward important methodological opportunities. Many studies rely on econometric modelling using secondary provincial datasets, while others employ evolutionary game theory or agent-based simulation. These approaches provide valuable macro-level insights but often overlook behavioural processes occurring within firms and supply chains. Future work could benefit from mixed-methods research combining quantitative analyses with qualitative case studies, participatory research, network analysis, and systems modelling. Such approaches would improve understanding of how technological innovations are adopted, negotiated, and institutionalized within complex agricultural systems.Looking ahead, several emerging technologies warrant greater scholarly attention. Although blockchain and artificial intelligence receive increasing coverage, relatively little empirical work has examined the integration of Internet of Things technologies, digital twins, edge computing, autonomous robotics, satellite-based monitoring, and generative artificial intelligence across agricultural value chains. Equally important is understanding how these technologies interact rather than evaluating them independently. Future studies should therefore move beyond single-technology assessments towards integrated digital ecosystem perspectives that recognise the complementarities among multiple technologies operating simultaneously within agricultural systems.Although most contributions are drawn from the Chinese context and rely primarily on cross-sectional empirical analyses or simulation-based methods, the studies presented in this Research Topic make a substantial contribution to the rapidly evolving literature on digital agriculture by demonstrating that digital transformation is fundamentally reshaping agribusiness systems, food value chains, and agricultural governance. Rather than treating digitalization as a purely technological phenomenon, the collection illustrates its multifaceted role in strengthening resilience, improving transparency, enhancing enterprise performance, facilitating market coordination, and promoting sustainable agricultural development. Importantly, the studies advance the field by integrating perspectives from agricultural economics, supply chain management, digital innovation, information systems, sustainability science, and institutional analysis. This interdisciplinary body of work provides robust empirical evidence that digital transformation is becoming a foundational pillar of modern food systems. At the same time, it highlights that realizing the full potential of digital agriculture will require greater attention to inclusiveness, governance, institutional capacity, and context-specific implementation. titel: Optimization of Microstructure and Pitting Corrosion Resistance in Laser‐Welded UNS S32001 Lean Duplex Stainless Steel Joints by Post Weld Heat Treatment
zusammenfassung: This study systematically investigates the effect of post‐weld heat treatment (PWHT) at 950–1250°C for 30 min on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of laser‐welded UNS S32001 lean duplex stainless steel (LDSS) joints. The as‐welded weld metal exhibits a ferrite‐dominated microstructure with an austenite content of only 20.7%. PWHT at 1050°C promotes balanced elemental diffusion and phase transformation kinetics, yielding a near‐equal ferrite‐austenite ratio (49.6% austenite) with a refined, equiaxed, and interwoven dual‐phase structure. In contrast, PWHT at 950°C retains undesirable Widmanstätten austenite (52.5% austenite), while higher temperatures (1150–1250°C) cause austenite dissolution (44.3% and 32.5%, respectively) and severe grain coarsening. Correspondingly, the specimen treated at 1050°C exhibits the best pitting corrosion resistance, with the highest critical pitting temperature (∼78.4°C vs. 71.1°C for as‐welded), the highest breakdown potential ( E b = 0.678 V SCE ), the lowest corrosion current density ( i corr = 4.175 × 10 −7 A·cm −2 ), and the largest polarization resistance ( R p = 283.9 kΩ·cm 2 ). This superior performance is attributed to the fine, homogeneous, interwoven dual‐phase structure, which enhances passive film stability, reduces localized electrochemical activity, and acts as an effective physical barrier against pit propagation.

titel: Comprehensive evaluation of AlphaFold/OpenFold prediction of experimentally unresolved proteins through novel metrics
zusammenfassung: Predicting accurate protein structures is essential for understanding molecular mechanisms, interpreting the impact of sequence variation, and supporting translational applications ranging from drug discovery to clinical genomics. Recent advances in deep-learning-based predictors such as AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 have transformed structural biology, enabling routine in silico modeling even for challenging or previously uncharacterized proteins. However, systematic benchmarking of these tools-especially for novel targets and single amino acid variants-remains limited. Conventional global metrics often fail to capture biologically meaningful discrepancies. By evaluating multiple implementations of AlphaFold2 and OpenFold, together with ColabFold and the AlphaFold3 server, across 10 different proteins and 222 single amino acid protein variants encompassing a wide range of sizes, structures, and functions, we show that although widely used global indicators-like mean pLDDT, pTM-score, and RMSD-frequently suggest comparable performance, substantial local-level differences remain elusive. To address this gap, we introduce a comparative framework leveraging Bland-Altman agreement analysis, to evaluate per-residue Cα-confidence differences and Per-Residue profiles (PRPs), complemented by Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP). This approach reveals marked localized divergences, particularly within flexible or intrinsically disordered regions, where both predictor choice and single-residue substitutions trigger the largest conformational shifts. We further demonstrate that using reduced homology databases has minimal impact on predicted structural quality, offering computationally efficient alternatives. Collectively, our findings underscore the importance of integrating global and residue-specific evaluations to more accurately assess robustness, agreement, and practical usability across contemporary protein structure prediction methods.

titel: Bundled Power: How Donors Value Procedural Powers in U.S. State Legislatures
zusammenfassung: ABSTRACT I examine the extent to which interest groups attend to institutional rules and procedures of lawmaking by assessing how they reward legislators who hold different forms of procedural authority in U.S. state legislatures. Revisiting an influential attempt to gauge interest group interest in procedural power, I reassess how “committee assignment power” has been measured and interpreted and ask what donors reward when they give to legislators coded as holding appointment authority. The analysis focuses on contributions directed toward actors involved in committee organization rather than direct access to committee members. I show that the contribution premium associated with assignment authority is composition sensitive and concentrated in a subset of chambers and leadership positions rather than uniformly observed across legislatures. Because offices involved in committee organization frequently bundle multiple procedural capacities, estimated assignment effects are difficult to attribute to appointment authority alone. The results suggest that donors reward bundled leadership capacities that structure the legislative agenda rather than committee appointment authority in isolation. More broadly, commonly used institutional measures may collapse multiple levers of power into a single indicator, and campaign finance may reinforce procedural centralization within legislatures as well as shape policy outcomes.

titel: Online Exposure and Its Effects on Psychosexual Health Among Youth
zusammenfassung: Objective: This article examines the impact of internet exposure and digital media engagement on the psychosexual well-being of adolescents and young adults. titel: Multi-dimensional assessment of parameters governing the thermal-humidity environment in high-geothermal tunnels during operation
zusammenfassung: The excessive heat and humidity in high-geothermal tunnels present significant challenges to personnel safety and structural stability. This study aimed to explore how geological and ventilation parameters influence thermal–humidity control performance of a tunnel during operation. An orthogonal test L27(3 6 ) was designed, incorporating three evaluation indices: the maximum temperature variation in the tunnel ( T D − v ), the heat index ( HI ), and the necessary ventilation duration ( t s ). The results indicate that the surrounding rock temperature exerts the most significant effect on T D − v , with a percentage contribution of 69.32%. The dominant parameter for the HI was found to be the air temperature, accounting for 81.83% of the variation. Regarding the t s index, both air temperature and surrounding rock temperature were identified as critical parameters, with contribution rates of 35.14% and 55.69%, respectively. Considering three indices, the significance of the parameters ranks is as follows: surrounding rock temperature, air temperature, surrounding rock thermal conductivity, ventilation time, fan speed, and relative humidity. The analysis yielded an optimal operational strategy with T D − v (5.35 °C), HI (12.79 °C), and t s (1 day).
