titel: Analysis of transient breakthroughs in fixed-bed adsorbers
zusammenfassung: The focus of this article is on the analysis of transient breakthrough experiments measured in laboratory scale units. The scale up of such breakthrough data to industrial scale Pressure Swing Adsorption (PSA) units requires simulations of the adsorption/desorption cycles in a sequence of multiple beds. This article provides a description of the simulation methodology that is essential for interpretation of laboratory scale data, and scaling up. A number of important conclusions are drawn from detailed analysis of large number of experimental breakthrough experiments, along with corresponding simulations. In the event that experimental breakthroughs are "sharp", this is a strong indication of the absence of intra-crystalline diffusion influences. A consequence of intra-crystalline diffusion influences is that breakthrough characteristics attain distended characteristics. Commonly, but not always, distended breakthroughs result in diminished produtivities of the desired product in mixture separation. In exceptional cases, intra-crystalline diffusion serves to complement and enhance the separations dictated by mixture equilibrium thermodynamics; such synergy manifests, for example, for 2MP/22DMB separations in MFI zeolite. For kinetically driven separations of C3H6/C3H8 mixtures using ZIF-8, and KAUST-7, both particle sizes and gas-particle contact times influence separations to a significant extent. The modelling of kinetically driven separations, requires thermodynamic coupling effects to be duly accounted for by use of the Maxwell-Stefan formulation for intra-crystalline diffusion.

titel: Gate2Code: Difficulty-Aware Planning and Code Generation for Arabic Tabular Question Answering
zusammenfassung: While large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive performance on free-text questions, their reliability on tabular question answering (Tabular QA) is constrained, especially for multi-step reasoning and numerical aggregation. titel: Pupillary adjustments to the illusory depth of rotoreliefs
zusammenfassung: Recent studies in the perception of visual illusions as well as mental imagery indicate that adjustments of the eye pupils reflect the perception instead of the light input stimulating the eyes. titel: The perils of penetration
zusammenfassung: The United States and China are engaged in what can best be described as a derisking race. Having encouraged their economies to become deeply intertwined, each nation is now attempting to achieve significant separation from the other. Neither side currently seeks to decouple completely. How the race plays out will be crucial to determining the outcome of the larger geopolitical contest of which it is part. As it intensifies, it will also reshape the world economy, halting the trend towards ever-tighter integration and fracturing the global system, most likely into a cluster of partially closed blocs. While its pace and outcome have yet to be determined, this process of fragmentation has already begun.

titel: Functional percolation:criticality of form and function
zusammenfassung: Abstract Understanding how network structure constrains and enables information processing is a central problem in statistical mechanics of interacting systems. Here, we study random networks across the structural percolation transition and analyze how connectivity governs realizable input–output transformations under cascade dynamics. Using Erdős–Rényi networks as a minimal ensemble, we examine structural, functional, and information-theoretic observables as functions of mean degree. We find that the emergence of the giant connected component coincides with a sharp transition in realizable information processing: complex input–output response functions become accessible, functional diversity increases rapidly, output entropy rises, and directed information flow—quantified by transfer entropy—extends beyond local neighborhoods. We term this coincidence of structural, functional, and informational transitions functional percolation, referring to a sharp expansion of the space of realizable input–output functions at the percolation threshold. Near criticality, networks exhibit a Pareto-optimal tradeoff between functional complexity and diversity, suggesting that percolation criticality may provide a general organizing principle of information processing capacity in systems with local interactions and propagating influences.

titel: Solar cooling technologies: a comparative review of thermal-driven and PV-driven systems, maturity, and deployment challenges
zusammenfassung: Growing cooling demands in hot, sunny areas are increasingly served by traditional electrically powered air conditioning, which adds to grid stress, fossil fuel use and greenhouse gas emissions. Solar cooling is a climatically well-matched alternative, as solar availability typically peaks at the same time as cooling load. The selected studies were classified into thermally and electrically driven families and critically compared using consistent metrics including coefficient of performance (COP), driving temperature, cooling capacity, collector type, storage requirement, cost, technological maturity and application scale. The review identifies solar absorption cooling as the most mature and widely deployed thermal-driven option, owing to its comparatively high COP (typically 0.6–1.3) and suitability for medium- to large-scale building applications. Although adsorption and desiccant systems enable lower-grade-heat operation and humidity control, they are constrained by larger system footprints and lower COP. Thermomechanical systems remain confined to experimental and pilot scales due to low efficiency, whereas PV-driven cooling is rapidly gaining ground as a modular, commercially mature alternative limited mainly by intermittency and storage cost. The novelty of this review lies in the comparison of the full spectrum of thermal and PV driven solar cooling technologies on a consistent set of technology-level metrics (driving temperature, cooling capacity, collector type, storage need, cycle-level COP, cost and maturity), and the linking of technology-specific barriers to concrete research gaps and stakeholder-oriented recommendations to accelerate the deployment of solar cooling.

titel: Translation of alcohol research to the academic medicine community
zusammenfassung: The goal of alcohol research is to improve overall health and well-being. Major advances have been made in the prevention and reduction of alcohol misuse, alcohol use disorder, and their consequences by (1) identifying patterns, trends, and public health impacts of alcohol misuse and designing effective interventions, (2) elucidating biological mechanisms of alcohol misuse and its consequences, including alcohol-related pathology, and (3) improving the diagnosis and treatment of alcohol use disorder and other alcohol-related conditions. Such efforts require an iterative process whereby the National Institutes of Health and NIAAA interact with medical schools and academic health systems of academic medicine to engage health professionals and health sciences students, clinical trainees, and faculty to meet these goals. Major challenges remain in translating fundamental research in diagnosis, prevention, and treatment into clinical practice in the academic medical community and into information for the public at large. titel: Fine-scale extraction of floating raft and cage aquaculture based on directional anisotropic feature enhancement
zusammenfassung: The spatial distribution mapping of floating raft aquaculture (FRA) and cage aquaculture (CA) is a critical task for fine-scale supervision of coastal waters. titel: Artificial intelligence and machine learning applications in drying systems: A comprehensive review
zusammenfassung: The industrial drying sector faces persistent challenges regarding energy inefficiency, nutrient degradation, and complex heat-mass transfer interactions. To mitigate these constraints, a systemic paradigm shift is transitioning dehydration technologies from rigid empirical models toward adaptive machine learning frameworks. Traditional mechanistic formulations suffer from high computational costs and estimation barriers, which severely limit online process control. Data-driven machine learning architectures, including artificial neural network (ANN) and deep learning models such as recurrent neural network (RNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, as well as deep-learning-enhanced model predictive control (MPC) strategies, offer superior accuracy in predicting process kinetics and reducing specific energy consumption. To address the data-dependency bottlenecks of pure black-box models, this paper critically examines the integration of physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), which mathematically enforce governing transport equations and boundary conditions directly within neural networks. Furthermore, the implementation of high-fidelity digital twins and real-time surrogate models is explored as a method to circumvent heavy computational overhead during complex porous-media and microwave interactions. Finally, this review addresses critical industrial challenges, emphasizing the urgent need for dataset standardization across research institutions and the strategic alignment of smart drying platforms with global carbon footprint reduction targets and United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs). Through this structured analysis, a structured computational roadmap is provided to guide the drying industry toward an autonomous, high-fidelity, and net-zero engineering future.

titel: The Purpose‐Driven Congress: Measuring and Explaining Legislative Outcomes of House Investigations

titel: Development and validation of the Emotional Gambling Scale (EGS) in a community sample from Spain with recent history of gambling
zusammenfassung: BACKGROUND: Difficulties in emotion regulation involving both positive and negative emotional states are central to gambling disorder. METHOD: The initial 55-item EGS used a five-point Likert scale. Following item analysis, 30 items were removed due to limited variability, extreme non-normality, or low item-total correlations, resulting in a final 25-item scale. The final version was administered to 371 Spanish-speaking individuals with recent gambling experience (mean age = 28.5, SD = 11.6; 54.4% male). Factor structure was examined using exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Internal consistency was evaluated via Cronbach's alpha and omega coefficients. Construct validity was assessed through correlations with gambling severity (NODS), gambling-related cognitions (GRCS-S), impulsivity (UPPS-P), anxiety and depression (HADS), and quality of life (QLI). RESULTS: Sampling adequacy was excellent (KMO = 0.93), and Bartlett's test of sphericity was significant, χ²(300) = 11,633.47, p < .001. EFA supported a two-factor structure comprising Positive Emotions (15 items) and Negative Emotions (10 items), explaining 70.8% of the variance. The factors were moderately correlated (r = .58). CFA supported the adequacy of the two-factor model, χ²(274) = 947.80, CFI = 0.993, TLI = 0.993, RMSEA = 0.082, and SRMR = 0.070. Standardized factor loadings ranged from 0.75 to 0.93. titel: Acting under uncertainty: Prediction, contingency, and the function of magic
zusammenfassung: For various reasons, the concept of magic has been disputed for several decades. Argued to be a pejorative assessment of other peoples' religious rites, magic is broadly understood as a vacuous concept without any explanatory value. While critique of former approaches is necessary, it is doubtful that terminological cleansing is helpful, or that dismantling distinctions such as that between magic and religion will make us any wiser. Building on previous work, I will present a bio-cultural approach to magical ritual focusing on its cognitive foundation as well as its functional role in negotiating tension arising between distinct levels of social organization, notably that between a ‘nurture sphere’, the extended family based on intimate-phatic communication, and a ‘community sphere’ consisting of coalitions between such families arbitrated by increasingly abstract, symbolic communication. Taking departure in a short discussion of previous explanatory approaches, I address the cognitive underpinning of magical action in a predictive processing framework. I then argue that magic addresses certain kinds of contingency events (e.g. illness or failure to procure sufficient food) that generate cognitive representations of a special ‘force’, and that magic applies this force to problems inherent to the nurture sphere. As contingency events affecting the survival of extended families potentially unbalance the relation between nurture spheres comprising a community, magic is argued to be part of cultural immune systems aimed to alleviate pressure arising from loyalties divided between family and group in the face of environmental pressures.

titel: Two-stage process combining N2O decomposition and ethane ODH over a MoVTeNbO-M1 catalyst

titel: Different age, different phenotype: a comparative analysis of juvenile and adult-onset dermatomyositis from a tertiary centre

titel: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry quantification of five antihistamines in antemortem blood: method validation and application

titel: Isoform-Specific TRIOBP Truncating Variants in Deafness, Autosomal Recessive 28: A Case Study of Postlingual Moderate Sensorineural Hearing Loss
ort: The Journal of Applied Laboratory Medicine
zusammenfassung: An 18-year-old Italian male was referred to the Audiology Service of AULSS3 Serenissima for evaluation of bilateral nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss. He was born to nonconsanguineous parents with normal hearing and had no family history of hearing impairment (Fig. 1, left panel). Pregnancy and perinatal history were unremarkable, with no reported infections or exposure to ototoxic agents. The patient first manifested hearing difficulties during childhood, and audiological follow-up has been ongoing since the age of 8 years. Pure-tone audiometry revealed a moderate, downsloping, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss (pure tone average at 500, 1000, 2000, and 4000 Hz: 44 dB), while the articulation gain curve showed a reduction in speech intelligibility consistent with the degree of hearing loss in both ears. After more than 10 years of follow-up, no progression of hearing loss has been observed to date. No additional abnormalities were noted in his clinical examination or medical history, and, therefore, a genetic etiology was suspected. The left panel shows the pedigree of the DFNB28 family. The solid black symbol represents the patient with stable, moderate, high-frequency hearing loss, while black dots denote unaffected carriers. The right panel displays the electropherograms of the truncating variants identified in the proband and his father; in addition to the paternal variant, the proband carries a second TRIOBP truncating variant, shown as an antisense electropherogram, which is consistent with maternal inheritance. Compound heterozygosity was indirectly demonstrated by inspection of the proband's read alignments (BAM file). In patients with stable and moderate postlingual sensorineural hearing loss, in the absence of syndromic features and recognized environmental risk factors, is it plausible to hypothesize a genetic etiology? Depending on the severity of sensorineural hearing loss, its time of onset, and the progression of hearing loss, is it plausible to assume that a specific transcript isoform of a specific deafness-related gene may be involved? Why is the identification of truncating variants limited to specific clinically relevant transcript isoforms impactful for variant interpretation, prognosis, and genetic counseling? Targeted next-generation sequencing analysis was performed using the Oto-GeneSGKit® v5 (Sistemas Genomicos), targeting 115 genes and miRNA-96 associated with hearing loss. Sequencing achieved an average coverage of >250×, with over 99.6% of targeted bases covered at least 20-fold. The sequences were aligned with the reference genome GRCh38/hg38. Sequence alignment, variant calling, and prioritization, in relation to the standards and guidelines drawn up by the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, were performed using CE-IVD Expert Variant Interpreter software (enGenome; https://evai.engenome.com). Copy number variant analysis was not included in the next-generation sequencing pipeline. The search for pathogenic, likely pathogenic, and variants of uncertain significance with minor allele frequency less than 0.05% in the Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Database build 157 and Genome Aggregation Database v4.1 (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/, accessed December 1, 2025) allowed us to identify 7 single-nucleotide variants. Among them, 2 truncated alleles in exon 9 of the TRIOBP gene (TRIO and F-actin binding protein; NM_001039141.3) were detected: c.4908delC/p.(Thr1637Profs*33), a previously unreported variant in individuals with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss type 28 (DFNB28; OMIM 609823) (1), exhibiting a minor allele frequency of 0.0003% in Genome Aggregation Database v4.1.0 [5/1604066 alleles; 22-37735242-GC-G(GRCh38)], with the highest allele frequency observed in the European (non-Finnish) population (5/1172532 alleles). The variant is not annotated in Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Database build 157. c.5014G>T/p.(Gly1672*), a known pathogenic variant that has been previously reported in a compound heterozygous state with other TRIOBP mutations in multiple individuals with DFNB28 (2–5) and that, as reported in Genome Aggregation Database v4.1.0, is the most frequent TRIOBP truncating variant [0.049%; 788/1613164 with one homozygous subject; 22-37735350-G-T(GRCh38)]. According to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology variant interpretation guidelines, the novel variant c.4908delC/p.(Thr1637Profs*33) was classified as likely pathogenic, supported by the criteria PVS1 (predicted null variant in a gene where loss of function is a known disease mechanism) and PM2_supporting (extremely low frequency in population databases), whereas c.5014G>T/p.(Gly1672*) was classified as pathogenic, supported by PVS1, PM2, and PP5 (reported as pathogenic in multiple reputable sources). To validate the causative genotype located in the long isoforms of the TRIOBP gene, a 307 bp PCR product was amplified from the genome DNA of available family members (the proband and his father). PCR amplification was performed using the forward primer 5′-CAGGGCTTTAGGGCCAGAG-3′ and the reverse primer 5′-GGGTGGAAACCTCCTTACCTG-3′, in combination with Platinum™ Taq DNA Polymerase (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The PCR fragments were purified, subjected to BigDye Terminator cycle sequencing, and then analyzed using an ABI PRISM 3500 genetic analyzer (Applied Biosystems; Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc.). The sequence reading was carefully examined and confirmed manually (Fig. 1, right panel). Inspection of the proband’s BAM file showed that the 2 variants are located on different sequencing reads, supporting a transconfiguration consistent with compound heterozygosity. TRIOBP is a well-established cause of DFNB28, classically associated with congenital, severe-to-profound prelingual hearing impairment. The gene encodes 4 main transcript isoforms: 2 long isoforms (TRIOBP-5 and TRIOBP-6) and 2 short isoforms (TRIOBP-1 and TRIOBP-4). The long isoforms contain coding regions encoded by exons that are not shared with the short isoforms, particularly exons 8–11, whereas the short isoforms overlap only with the N-terminal (TRIOBP-4) or C-terminal (TRIOBP-1) portions of the long transcripts. This complex transcript architecture underlies important functional differences among isoforms and has significant implications for genotype–phenotype correlations. Most pathogenic TRIOBP variants reported to date cluster in exon 7; disrupt both long and short isoforms, including TRIOBP-4; and are typically associated with the classic DFNB28 phenotype, a form of prelingual, severe-to-profound nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss (1). In contrast, some studies have described milder and often postlingual phenotypes in individuals carrying at least one allele selectively affecting only the long isoforms (TRIOBP-5/6), while preserving expression of the short isoforms (2–4). The present case further expands this emerging paradigm by demonstrating that biallelic truncating variants restricted exclusively to the long isoform–specific coding regions are sufficient to cause DFNB28, albeit with a distinctly milder, stable, and high-frequency–predominant audiological profile. Interestingly, the human DFNB28 phenotype associated with the presence of at least one truncating variant affecting the long isoforms only of TRIOBP [this study and (2–4)] partially overlaps with the auditory phenotype observed in TRIOBP-5 knockout mice (6). In both species, hearing loss is moderate and predominantly involves high frequencies. In humans, the deficit is typically restricted to high frequencies and remains stable over time, whereas in TRIOBP-5 knockout mice, hearing loss initially affects high frequencies and progressively worsens, eventually involving all tested frequencies. This phenotypic divergence likely reflects species-specific differences in cochlear rootlet architecture (7) and potentially distinct compensatory mechanisms, such as differential expression and regulation of TRIOBP isoforms during inner ear development. Multiple sequence alignment confirmed that the region harboring the identified variants is unique to TRIOBP-5/6 and absent from TRIOBP-1 and TRIOBP-4 (Fig. 2). This finding provides a molecular basis for the observed phenotype and supports the concept that isoform-level pathogenicity can generate distinct phenotypic subtypes. For example, in cardiovascular genetics, the impact of truncating variants in the TTN gene depends strongly on exon/isoform inclusion (different effects for long N2BA vs short N2B isoforms), with important consequences for dilated cardiomyopathy risk stratification (8). Multiple sequence alignment of the short (TRIOBP-1 [NP_008963.3] and TRIOBP-4 [ABB59560.1]) and long (TRIOBP-5 [ABB59559.1] and TRIOBP-6 [NP_001034230.1]) isoforms of TRIOBP. The alignment shows that the causative variants identified in the proband, p.(Thr1637Profs*33) and p.(Gly1672*), are located between amino acids 1354 and 1702 of NP_001034230.1 (in bold), corresponding to the genomic region encoded by exon 9, which is exclusive to long isoforms. The amino acids Thr1637 and Gly1672 are shown in red. In the context of our findings, the observation that selective disruption of TRIOBP-5/6 leads to a milder phenotype suggests that residual expression of TRIOBP-1/4 may preserve essential cytoskeletal functions in inner ear cells, thereby offering a rationale for isoform-targeted therapeutic strategies. Given that our patient’s variants introduce premature stop codons in long-isoform–specific exon 9, future interventions should focus on restoring full-length TRIOBP-5/6 expression or compensating for its loss. Recent advances in the field support this translational potential: gene therapy using adeno-associated virus vectors for autosomal recessive nonsyndromic deafness has entered early clinical trials (e.g., adeno-associated virus–otoferlin in autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss, locus 41), showing meaningful hearing improvement in children (9). Furthermore, in vivo genome editing in adult mouse models of hereditary deafness (e.g., adeno-associated virus–CRISPR-associated protein 9–single-guide RNA in an autosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss, locus 41 model) has successfully restored auditory and vestibular function, underlining the feasibility of targeted gene correction in the inner ear (10). In the specific context of DFNB28, selective restoring of TRIOBP-5/6 while sparing TRIOBP-1/4 may represent a personalized therapeutic avenue that aligns with the observed genotype–phenotype correlation and offers a strategic window for intervention. From a diagnostic laboratory perspective, this case underscores the importance of transcript-aware variant interpretation in next-generation sequencing workflows. Conventional gene-level classification alone may obscure clinically meaningful distinctions driven by isoform-specific effects. Incorporating isoform structure into variant interpretation can refine prognostic assessment, improve genotype–phenotype correlations, and support more accurate genetic counseling. Finally, recognition of isoform-restricted pathogenicity has potential translational implications. Preservation of TRIOBP-1/4 expression in this patient may confer partial functional compensation within the cochlear cytoskeleton, contributing to the milder phenotype. This observation raises the possibility that future therapeutic strategies, such as readthrough approaches for premature termination codons or isoform-specific gene replacement, could selectively restore TRIOBP-5/6 function while sparing essential short isoforms. TRIOBP-related DFNB28 encompasses a broader phenotypic spectrum than classically recognized, with disease severity influenced by transcript isoform involvement. Truncating variants selectively affecting the long TRIOBP isoforms (TRIOBP-5/6) are associated with milder, postlingual, and stable hearing loss compared with variants disrupting both long and short isoforms. Isoform-aware interpretation of next-generation sequencing results is essential to avoid oversimplified genotype–phenotype correlations in hereditary hearing loss. Incorporating transcript structure into diagnostic workflows can improve prognostic assessment and support the development of precision, isoform-targeted therapeutic strategies. titel: Association of the Fibrosis-4 index with thyroid nodule prevalence in women: a cross-sectional study
zusammenfassung: BACKGROUND: The relationship between liver-related metabolic markers and thyroid nodules (TNs) has attracted increasing interest. However, whether the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index is independently associated with TN prevalence in women, particularly after accounting for the age embedded in the score, remains unclear. We investigated the association between FIB-4 and prevalent TNs in a female health-check cohort and assessed its robustness in age-stratified and age-adjusted analyses. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 695 women from a health examination cohort at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University. TNs were defined as ultrasound-detected thyroid nodules. Multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for prevalent TNs according to standardized FIB-4 levels. Prespecified age-stratified analyses were performed for women aged ≤ 60 years and > 60 years. Within each age stratum, an additional model adjusted for continuous age. Age-adjusted within-stratum results were considered the main basis for interpretation. RESULTS: In the full female cohort, the association between FIB-4 and prevalent TNs was attenuated after additional adjustment for continuous age (OR 1.104, 95% CI 0.822-1.484; P = 0.511). In age-adjusted within-stratum analyses, FIB-4 was not significantly associated with prevalent TNs in either women aged ≤ 60 years (OR 1.211, 95% CI 0.837-1.751; P = 0.310) or women aged > 60 years (OR 0.567, 95% CI 0.289-1.113; P = 0.099). The corresponding base model estimates before additional continuous-age adjustment were OR 1.564 (95% CI 1.086-2.253; P = 0.016) and OR 0.576 (95% CI 0.278-1.193; P = 0.138), respectively. The interaction between FIB-4 and age group was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.239). CONCLUSIONS: After additional adjustment for continuous age within age strata, the association between FIB-4 and prevalent thyroid nodules in women was attenuated and no longer statistically significant. These findings suggest that the apparent relationship between FIB-4 and TN prevalence in this health-check population may be substantially influenced by age handling and should be interpreted cautiously. titel: When the evolved social mind goes online: How digital ecologies recalibrate mentalizing and social bonding
zusammenfassung: Humans are an ultra-social species whose psychological architecture was shaped in environments characterized by repeated interaction, bodily co-presence, and rich streams of social information (Balconi, 2025;Barkow et al., 1992;Dunbar & Shultz, 2007;Lim & Tan, 2024). Paradoxically, a growing proportion of affiliative, romantic, and friendship processes now unfold through messaging platforms, social media, and video-mediated communication (Doheny & Lighthall, 2023;Frampton & Fox, 2018). Yet despite rapid empirical growth, the field still lacks an integrated evolutionary account of how these environments alter the mechanisms that support social inference, attachment, and shared closeness (Murni et al., 2025;van Vugt et al., 2024). As we argue here, digital ecologies do not create entirely new social minds, but recalibrate evolved mechanisms underlying mentalizing, attachment, and interpersonal affection (Farkas, 2024;Feldman, 2017;Wolf & Tomasello, 2025).The key issue is not simply that digital technologies are new, but that they systematically alter the context on which the human social mind depends, such as that "people today interact with the Digital Age world using their Stone Age brains designed to confront problems specific to an ancient environment" (Chang & Durante, 2022, p. 1). That is an evolutionary problem because minds adapted for embodied interaction are increasingly required to operate on thinner, delayed, and technologically filtered social signals (Timilsina, 2025). Here, we propose a three-part framework in which Theory of Mind (ToM) is the upstream inferential system, attachment is the regulatory system, and interpersonal closeness is a downstream relational outcome. Figure 1 summarizes the proposed framework. Digital ecologies are conceptualized as transformed cue environments that recalibrate, rather than replace, evolved mechanisms of mentalizing, attachment regulation, interpersonal emotion, and social bonding. A useful starting point is the observation that mentalizing, attachment, and bonding ordinarily operate in coordinated fashion (Wolf & Tomasello, 2025). ToM supports inferences about others' beliefs, intentions, emotions, and responsiveness (Cosmides et al., 2010). Attachment regulation manages proximity, safety, reassurance, and distress (Bączkowski & Cierpiałkowska, 2015;Mikulincer & Shaver, 2016). Interpersonal closeness concerns the extent to which another person is integrated into the self; Inclusion of Other in the Self (IOS) has been associated with pair-bonding, self-expansion, and cognitive interdependence (Branand et al., 2019). These systems evolved in informationally rich settings. Physical touch is one of the clearest examples (Saluja et al., 2024). In Harlow's classic experiments, infant rhesus monkeys strongly preferred a soft cloth surrogate mother over a wire one that provided food, supporting the conclusion that contact comfort is foundational rather than secondary to attachment (Harlow, 1958). More recent work extends that logic across primates, arguing that social and affective touch contribute to alliance formation, emotional stability, and social cohesion (Jablonski, 2021), which is consistent with the multiple benefits of touch that have been documented in humans (Morrison & Croy, 2021;Packheiser et al., 2024).Direct eye contact is another core input. Hietanen's (2018) integrative review shows that direct gaze has robust effects on attention and affective processing. Face-to-face interaction also includes the real-time sharing of facial expressions, posture, prosody, and temporal synchrony, allowing social judgments to be assembled from multiple converging signals simultaneously (Carmichael & Mizrahi, 2024;Kopp, 2010).Digital ecologies can be defined as socio-technical environments composed of platforms, interfaces, algorithms, and networked users that shape the flow, visibility, timing, and salience of social information (Skog et al., 2018). Their relevance to the evolved social mind becomes clearer: digital interaction does not remove social information, but it often reshapes it away from high-fidelity face-to-face channels and toward thinner, delayed, curated, or platform-shaped signals. In this way, human perception and cognition are being progressively recalibrated by digital environments (Kirjakovski, 2023).Language also occupies a distinctive position within digital ecologies. Unlike many face-to-face interactions, which distribute social information across multiple embodied channels, digitally mediated exchanges often rely heavily on linguistic and symbolic cues (Magni et al., 2025). In such contexts, language functions not merely as a vehicle for communication but as a primary ecological resource through which individuals construct representations of others' intentions, emotions, and relational states (Kravchenko, 2025). Consequently, digital interaction may increase dependence on linguistic interpretation while reducing access to the embodied cues that ordinarily constrain social inference.Three changes are especially important. First, ordinary digital interaction removes physical contact entirely (Saini et al., 2024). Second, it often disrupts genuine eye contact (Kaiser et al., 2022). Research on videoconferencing and online interview settings shows that camera-screen geometry makes natural mutual gaze difficult: users typically cannot both look at the partner's onscreen face and align their gaze with the camera (Schmitz et al., 2023). Studies have also shown that off-camera gaze can reduce social evaluations in online contexts, and recent work in video interviews suggests that perceived eye contact affects how applicants are judged (Basch & Melchers, 2025;Shinya et al., 2024). Third, facial expression sharing becomes partial and technologically filtered rather than embedded in a fully shared physical context (Parkinson, 2008).However, these limitations should not be interpreted as evidence that digital interaction simply weakens interpersonal emotion or social connection. Rather, recent findings suggest that digital and remote interactions reorganize the feedback conditions through which emotion is expressed, perceived, maintained, and adjusted. Virtual interactions can still generate spontaneous interpersonal coordination: for example, motor synchrony and emotional alignment have been observed in Zoom interactions between strangers, alongside increases in trust, liking, cohesion, self-other overlap, and perceived similarity (Gvirts et al., 2023). Similarly, emotional contagion can occur in dyadic online video conferences. However, the transmission of emotion may differ across emotional categories and may not always be fully captured by visible facial expression, particularly for negative emotions (Marx et al., 2025). These findings suggest that remote interaction does not eliminate socio-affective attunement, but changes the channels through which it becomes available.At the same time, different modes of remote contact appear to afford different styles of emotional coordination. In-person, video, and audio communication differ in cognitive effort, emotional intensity, and dyadic synchronization, with in-person interaction showing stronger synchronization of positive emotions than video communication, while audio-only interaction may sustain emotional intensity in distinctive ways (Han et al., 2024). Social media platforms further shape emotional regulation through their affordances: selectivity can support intrapersonal regulation, visibility can structure emotional self-presentation, bandwidth can influence interpersonal regulation, and connectivity can enable collective emotion regulation (Peng et al., 2024). Digital expressive tools such as emojis, emoticons, GIFs, stickers, and memes may also compensate for the loss of embodied cues while creating novel forms of relational warmth, playfulness, affective nuance, and emotional creativity (Cavalheiro et al., 2024;Ju, 2024;Peng, 2025).This means digital interaction is far from the sensory conditions under which bonding mechanisms evolved (Feldman, 2017). It is less tactile, less gaze-coherent, and often less synchronously embodied (Farkas, 2024). The result is not an absence of social cognition, but a redistribution of social information toward more ambiguous and inferentially demanding inputs (Doheny & Lighthall, 2023). In this sense, digital ecologies may recalibrate rather than replace evolved mechanisms for interpersonal bonding: they reduce some embodied cues that support attachment, synchrony, and responsiveness, while introducing new symbolic, temporal, and platform-mediated cues through which people attempt to maintain emotional alignment, regulate relational uncertainty, and creatively reconstruct social connection.ToM should be central to this framework because it sits upstream of many downstream relational outcomes (Wolf & Tomasello, 2025). In face-to-face interaction, social understanding is not solely a matter of explicit inference, but is often grounded in a second-person mode of engagement characterized by direct reciprocity and embodied co-regulation (Barone & Gomila, 2021;Pérez & Gomila, 2021;Schilbach et al., 2013). Under these conditions, mentalizing is scaffolded by direct gaze, facial movement, touch, prosody, timing, and shared context, allowing many social inferences to occur rapidly and implicitly (Hamilton & Holler, 2023).In digital ecologies, by contrast, individuals must often infer internal states from fewer cues, less reliable timing, and weaker embodied grounding (Kirjakovski, 2023). In many cases, these inferences must be derived primarily from linguistic exchanges, making the interpretation of written language an increasingly important component of mentalizing in digital environments. By disrupting real-time reciprocal engagement, digitally mediated communication may shift social cognition away from relatively automatic second-person processes and toward more explicit and effortful forms of inferential mindreading (Wiltshire et al., 2015). Rather than directly perceiving others' intentions or affective states through embodied interaction, individuals increasingly reconstruct them from fragmented, delayed, and context-poor signals. This dynamic becomes particularly evident in text-based and group messaging environments, where the absence of mutually oriented embodied behaviors often requires individuals to imagine or assume the states, intentions, and positions of others rather than perceive them directly. Druzhinin and Ramirez (2026) argue that such conditions may foster a dysfunctional human-environment cognitive ecology, in which interpretations become increasingly detached from the perceptual grounding ordinarily provided by embodied interaction. Doheny and Lighthall (2023) note that remote interpersonal communication changes the social-cognitive conditions under which people process social stimuli, social reward, rejection, and higher-level cognition, including ToM. In digital environments, individuals may therefore rely more heavily on inferential processes to form beliefs about others' internal states from limited information (Pascarelli et al., 2023). Evidence that text-based communication recruits greater activation in brain regions associated with explicit mentalizing, particularly the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, relative to face-to-face interaction is consistent with the idea that digitally mediated exchanges place greater demands on interpretive systems (Sacristan et al., 2023). This increased reliance on inference creates a distinct cognitive environment in which digital platforms do not merely mirror, but transform, traditional relational dynamics (Hutchison et al., 2025). This is our central theoretical move: digital ecologies do not eliminate mentalizing demands; rather, they may intensify them while making accurate inference more difficult. Under such conditions, delayed replies, ambiguous online interactions, and context-poor signals may require disproportionate interpretive work, increasing cognitive load and facilitating repetitive cycles of social interpretation.Therefore, we suggest a cautious but strong claim: digital ecologies likely increase inferential ambiguity and load in mentalizing systems. This does not by itself prove a universal bias toward jealousy or threat. Still, it offers a plausible explanation for why attachment-related vigilance, reassurance-seeking, and hypermentalizing may become easier to trigger in digitally mediated relationships (Goetz et al., 2019).Because attachment regulation depends partly on how people infer others' availability, responsiveness, and warmth, changes in mentalizing should propagate downstream into attachment processes (Bowlby, 1982). Mentalizing is rooted in early attachment experiences, which shape the socio-affective knowledge required to interpret social interactions (Vannucci & Tottenham, 2025). Since contact comfort is foundational, communication systems that remove physical contact also remove one of the primate-evolved substrates of felt safety (Harlow, 1958). If direct gaze supports mutual attunement, then systems that interrupt eye contact may weaken another major input into perceived responsiveness (Hietanen, 2018). In combination, these changes may alter how security is established and maintained in close relationships (Bączkowski & Cierpiałkowska, 2015).Insecure attachment styles can contribute to relational instability, whereas effective partner regulation can enhance emotional responses and relationship satisfaction, demonstrating the interplay between attachment and mentalizing (Overall & Simpson, 2015). Furthermore, the development of mentalizing is linked to early caregiver interactions, which foster emotional self-regulation and the capacity to navigate complex social environments (Gergely & Unoka, 2008;Sharp et al., 2020). This perspective also sharpens the relevance of IOS. Interpersonal closeness is not merely a function of how often two people interact; it involves overlap, mutual incorporation, and cognitive-emotional interdependence (Aron et al., 1992). A central proposition of this paper is that digital abundance of contact may coexist with fragility in perceived cognitive overlap. By cognitive overlap, we refer to the subjective perception that one's thoughts, intentions, emotions, and interpretations are mutually understood and sufficiently aligned with those of another person. Importantly, this overlap reflects a sense of shared understanding rather than actual equivalence of mental states. When mutual attunement depends on degraded cuesfoot_0 , self-other overlap may become more unstable (Branand et al., 2019), fluctuating with uncertainty and interpretive strain rather than being anchored in rich embodied exchange.Viewing digital interaction through an evolutionary lens offers two advantages. First, it avoids the simplistic claim that online relationships are unreal, socially empty, or necessarily impoverished. The argument is not that digital communication lacks social significance, but that it modifies the cue structure that evolved mechanisms were forged to respond to. Second, it generates empirically tractable questions. Under what conditions can video-mediated communication partially restore gaze-based attunement? Which symbolic cues best compensate for the absence of touch? Do attachment style or social sensitivity moderate the effects of degraded cues on mentalizing? To what extent do linguistic environments themselves shape mentalizing processes and perceived interpersonal understanding in digitally mediated relationships? And can self-other overlap be sustained digitally without bodily co-presence, or does it become more dependent on platform-specific forms of reassurance, emotional synchrony, and expressive creativity? (Basch et al., 2025;Doheny & Lighthall, 2023;Gvirts et al., 2023;Schmitz et al., 2023).More broadly, this framework is useful because it links classic attachment insights, contemporary social neuroscience, emotion research, and relationship theory. Harlow's work highlighted the primacy of contact comfort (Harlow, 1958). Gaze research shows that mutual eye contact supports affective and attentional alignment (Hietanen, 2018). Digital social neuroscience suggests that remote communication changes the sensory and inferential basis of higher-level social cognition (Doheny & Lighthall, 2023). Recent work on virtual synchrony, emotional contagion, social media affordances, and emoji-based interaction further suggests that digital environments do not eliminate socio-affective attunement, but reorganize its channels and expressive forms (Cavalheiro et al., 2024;Han et al., 2024;Marx et al., 2025;Peng et al., 2024). IOS research reminds us that closeness is not reducible to frequency of interaction (Branand et al., 2019). Taken together, these literatures support the conclusion that digital ecologies pose an evolutionary challenge by altering the sensory foundations of bonding while leaving affiliative needs intact. Future work should further examine the ecological role of language in digitally mediated relationships, particularly how linguistic interaction contributes to the construction of social reality and interpersonal understanding under conditions of reduced embodied access.Human social cognition evolved for embodied, multimodal, and mutually regulated interaction, not merely for the exchange of propositional information. Contact comfort, affective touch, direct gaze, facial expression sharing, and temporal synchrony help anchor mentalizing, attachment, and closeness in ordinary face-to-face life (Harlow, 1958;Hietanen, 2018;Jablonski, 2021;Packheiser et al., 2024). Digital ecologies do not create new social minds; they recalibrate evolved mechanisms of mentalizing, attachment, interpersonal emotion, and closeness by changing the timing, richness, and reliability of the cues those mechanisms evolved to process. That is why digital connection can feel socially dense yet affectively unstable: abundant in contact, sometimes fragile in embodied attunement, but also capable of generating new forms of symbolic reassurance, emotional alignment, and relational creativity.

titel: Fabrication of Beeswax–Soapwort Root Powder–Gelatin Bigel-Based Foamed Emulsions for Use as a Fat Replacer in Mousse
zusammenfassung: In this study, beeswax (BW) and gelatin, soapwort root powder (SRP) were employed to create oleogel and hydrogel for bigel development, respectively. The study aimed to determine the potential utilization of SRP in the bigel system to create a novel fat replacer (bigel-based foamed emulsion) for mousse production. Bigels with 2% SRP showed a bicontinuous emulsion structure. The FTIR spectra of all the bigels exhibited no new peaks. Bigels had solid-like properties, given that no crossover point was present and G′ values were uniformly greater than G″ values. Hardness, gumminess, and chewiness were improved by increasing the bigel’s gelatin and SRP concentrations. A rise in the SRP ratio and gelatin content resulted in a higher overrun of bigel-based foamed emulsions. An increment in the SRP ratio resulted in enhanced thermal stability, with the exception of 9% G-2. The G′ values surpassed the G″ values, indicating that the mousse samples exhibited solid-like characteristics. From the prepared samples, 6% G-2 M was determined to be the closest to the control mousse in terms of hardness, springiness, cohesiveness, and gumminess values when comparing the bigel mousse samples with the control mousse sample (p > 0.05). The 6% G-2 M sample showed the lowest ΔE* value and was the closest sample to CM.

titel: Landscape, law and justice as longue durée history – Norwegian medieval laws and their long-term legacy
zusammenfassung: Norway celebrated in 2024 the 750th anniversary of Magnus the Lawmender’s Law of the Realm or Magnus Code. Norway was the third realm in medieval Europe to promulgate a unified law code for the whole land and the first where it was effective. The code was derived from case law in older medieval provincial laws, Canon Law and new royal legislation. It remained in force, with modifications, until 1687, and some provisions are recognisable in present-day law. This article explores how landscape, law and justice were interrelated in Norway’s medieval laws, and how far continuing aspects of this relationship constitute longue durée history. The article examines legislation concerning land rights and use of landscape resources. Enduring dimensions of landscape justice are found in evolving legislation on rights of kin (odelsrett), land inheritance, land reorganisation, commons, and rights of access, despite the changing role of ‘things’ (courts) as judicial institutions.

titel: WHO TAUGHT YOU WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE?
zusammenfassung: Abstract The author is a professional speaker and entrepreneur who started a reselling business at 19 while studying Psychology at Duke University. Originally, it began as a “side hustle.” It became a six‐figure business, and the basis for great personal satisfaction. She describes the origins and current status of the “side hustle” term, and notes that she initially kept her business a secret. She didn't believe it fit in with a fast‐moving professional career, in which she had “published 3 books by 21, facilitated workshops for companies like Netflix and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, was an International Coaching Federation certified coach, and wrote for Psychology Today .” She didn't learn to attribute more pride to her entrepreneurship until after college, with the help of her coach: “The image of success was passed down through ranking systems, report cards, job titles, and bank statements. Most of us absorbed this idea so completely and so subconsciously that we never thought to question whether it was what we actually believed.”

titel: Whom Do Chief Ministers Serve?
zusammenfassung: Chief ministers in India play among the most important roles in determining access to a wide range of public services. Do chief ministers use the power of their office to enhance public service delivery broadly across the states in which they govern? Or do they more narrowly direct resources towards the individual constituencies they represent and in which they must seek re-election? Using a geographical proximity design, we examine new data covering 1992 to 2012 to study the impact of chief minister representation on a constituency’s access to electricity and find clear variations in distribution strategies across states. We find that chief ministers target their constituencies with increases in electricity supply. These variations in public service targeting are driven by differences in institutional environment and political security of India’s chief ministers. We also find some evidence of short-term positive spillovers in the local region.

titel: The dangers of dependence
zusammenfassung: The United States and China are engaged in what can best be described as a derisking race. Having encouraged their economies to become deeply intertwined, each nation is now attempting to achieve significant separation from the other. Neither side currently seeks to decouple completely. Instead, each is trying to alter the terms of their economic relationship, reducing its own vulnerability to leverage, coercion or attacks that could damage its prosperity and security, while working to maintain or acquire advantages over its counterparty.In this Adelphi book, Aaron Friedberg argues that the derisking race is thus a struggle for power, waged in the realms of trade, investment and technology development; it is the economic dimension of the all-encompassing political, military and ideological ‘systemic rivalry’ now under way. How the race plays out will be crucial to determining the outcome of the larger geopolitical contest of which it is part. As it intensifies, it will also reshape the world economy, halting the trend towards ever-tighter integration and fracturing the global system, most likely into a cluster of partially closed blocs. While its pace and outcome have yet to be determined, this process of fragmentation has already begun.

titel: Acute parvovirus B19-associated inflammatory musculoskeletal disease: clinical phenotypes and remission trajectories from the GIRRCS network
zusammenfassung: OBJECTIVE: To describe clinical phenotype, selected imaging findings and remission trajectories in adults with acute parvovirus B19-associated inflammatory musculoskeletal disease referred for rheumatological assessment. METHODS: This was a non-interventional multicentre observational study in GIRRCS rheumatology units. Adults with new-onset inflammatory musculoskeletal manifestations, positive anti-parvovirus B19 IgM and symptom onset within 4 weeks were enrolled. Clinical, laboratory and clinically indicated imaging data were collected. Time to first documented clinical remission was defined as the interval from symptom onset to the first rheumatologist-confirmed assessment showing resolution of inflammatory musculoskeletal manifestations. Patients requiring disease-modifying escalation were analysed separately. RESULTS: Twenty-four adults were enrolled; 18 were women (75.0%) and mean age was 44.4 ± 14.8 years. Clinical involvement was polyarticular in 14 patients (58.3%) and oligoarticular in 10 (41.7%); enthesitis occurred in 4 (16.7%) and dactylitis was absent. Inflammatory markers were modestly elevated, and most patients with complete autoantibody data were seronegative. Imaging was performed selectively and documented inflammatory abnormalities in clinically indicated examinations. Follow-up data were available for 21 patients, of whom 20 (95.2%) achieved clinical remission without DMARD escalation; median documented remission timing was 21 days (IQR 10-60; range 7-135). One patient required biologic escalation for persistent inflammatory disease. Exploratory regression analyses did not identify robust associations with documented remission timing. CONCLUSION: Acute parvovirus B19-associated inflammatory musculoskeletal disease may mimic inflammatory rheumatic disease in adults referred for rheumatological assessment. Most patients achieved remission without disease-modifying escalation, although remission timing varied and one patient required biologic therapy for persistent inflammatory disease.

titel: Triple primary synchronous liver cancer in one patient: the first case report and origin speculation through bioinformatics
zusammenfassung: INTRODUCTION: A diagnosis of multiple primary liver tumors is extremely rare. Preoperative diagnosis based on imaging findings is difficult. Moreover, the clinical benefits of treatment strategies for multiple liver cancers remain unclear. Here, we report a case of three synchronous primary liver tumors with three distinct pathological types-hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), and combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC‑CCA)-in a single patient. Bioinformatics analysis supported at least two clonal origins, with cHCC‑CCA and ICC sharing a common lineage based on identical HBV integration sites. CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old female with a history of hepatitis B for several years presented with three lesions in hepatic segment VIII. Multiphase magnetic resonance imaging with gadolinium ethoxybenzyl diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid revealed a diagnosis of multiple lesions, namely, cHCC‑CCA, with multiple intrahepatic metastases. The AFP level was normal, while the CA 19 - 9 level was mildly elevated (normal range ≤ 30.00 U/ml). Hepatectomy was performed, and postoperative assessment confirmed that the large lesion was cHCC‑CCA. However, the small lesions close to the large lesion were HCC and ICC. Gene testing revealed distinct mutational profiles among the three tumors. Similar gene mutations were detected in cHCC‑CCA and ICC. We also found that gene fragments of hepatitis B virus-C (HBV-C) were inserted into the genomes of ICC and cHCC‑CCA rather than that of HCC. The genomic integration site of HBV-C in cHCC‑CCA and ICC was the same. CONCLUSION: We report an extremely rare case of three synchronous primary liver tumors with three distinct pathological types (HCC, ICC, and cHCC‑CCA) in a single patient. Bioinformatics analysis supported at least two clonal origins, with cHCC‑CCA and ICC sharing a common lineage based on identical HBV integration sites. Hepatectomy represents a potential radical strategy for the treatment of multiple PLCs.

titel: Assessment practices resistant to inappropriate AI use in Open Distance eLearning: insights from Zimbabwe Open University
zusammenfassung: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into educational practices has raised significant concerns among educators regarding the integrity and effectiveness of traditional assessment methods in the Zimbabwean education sector. This has raised concerns regarding the reliability of submitted assignments, research articles, research projects and other formative assessments, especially as some students use AI to write assignments and other academic tasks. Accordingly, this paper sought to identify assessment practices perceived as effective in promoting authentic student learning and minimizing the inappropriate use of artificial intelligence in Open Distance eLearning environments. A qualitative and instrumental case study design was employed with in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Seven lecturers, fourteen students and a quality assurance coordinator were purposively sampled from the Masvingo Regional Campus of the Zimbabwe Open University. This study used Constructivist Learning Theory (Piaget, Vygotsky), as lens to understand effective assessment strategies that minimize inappropriate use of artificial intelligence. The findings indicate that in class tests/ assignments, presentations, creation of tasks that can be assessed by observation of student performance, interviews and engaging students in debates, panel discussions and seminars that require students to prepare their arguments and support them can be resistant to inappropriate use of Artificial Intelligence in Open Distance learning. The study suggests that efforts should be made to incorporate artificial intelligence into teacher training curricula in colleges and universities to maintain academic integrity.

titel: Effectiveness of peer-led sexuality education in reducing risky sexual behaviors among adolescents attending secondary schools in Masaka City, Uganda
ort: International Journal of Adolescence and Youth
zusammenfassung: Adolescents in Uganda continue to experience high levels of risky sexual behaviours despite existing school‑based sexuality education programmes, with limited evidence on the effectiveness of peer‑led approaches. This study examined the effectiveness of peer‑led sexuality education on sexual behaviours among secondary school adolescents in Masaka City, Uganda. A two-arm cluster randomized controlled trial (cRCT), reported in accordance with CONSORT guidelines, was conducted among 912 students from eight secondary schools in Masaka City, Uganda. The intervention group received an eight‑week peer‑led sexuality education programme. Data were collected at baseline, post‑intervention, and three‑month follow‑up. The intervention significantly increased sexual abstinence (aOR = 2.070; p < 0.001) and reduced multiple sexual partnerships (aOR = 0.460; p < 0.001), alcohol/drug use (aOR = 0.440; p = 0.001), and unprotected sex. Peer-led sexuality education is an effective strategy for improving adolescent sexual behaviours. Participants reported high levels of satisfaction with the intervention.

titel: Co-Constructing Intercultural CLIL: A Multilevel, Dynamic Model for Language, Cultural Identity, and Pedagogical Practice in a CLIL-Focused Chinese University
zusammenfassung: This study examines the potential of Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) in Chinese higher education to develop Intercultural Communicative Competence (ICC) by challenging monolingual ideologies and negotiating cultural identities—an underexplored dimension, as existing research has primarily addressed CLIL’s effectiveness in language and subject learning. Based on an exploratory case study at a CLIL-focused Chinese university, this study draws on document analysis of national education policies, teacher training programmes, and course syllabi, along with semi-structured interviews with 12 experienced CLIL educators. Thematic analysis demonstrates CLIL’s effectiveness in developing communicative competence, intercultural knowledge, awareness, and behaviours, advancing pluriliteracies across linguistic and cultural contexts. These findings inform a practice-oriented model for Chinese higher education, revealing CLIL as both a pedagogical approach and a medium for reshaping cultural identities. The model is co-constructed through drawing on and triangulating macro-meso documentary discourses with micro-level practitioner accounts, informing context-sensitive, identity-responsive language education reform in CLIL curriculum design and teacher development.

titel: Underrepresentation of Women CEOs
zusammenfassung: Abstract Why do so few women become CEOs? To understand this glass ceiling, we estimate a dynamic model of the CEO gender decision, which contains perceived gender productivity differences, search costs reflecting limited female labor supply, and employer disutility from discrimination. The key factor is the shortage of suitable female candidates, as boards prefer hiring women, and productivity differences between genders are minimal. We find no evidence of a glass cliff in which women become CEOs just as firms are failing. While better governance is associated with women becoming CEOs, the importance of limited female labor supply is unrelated to governance.

titel: Incorporating research advisory groups in speech-language therapy research in Aotearoa New Zealand: a scoping review
zusammenfassung: Speech-language therapy (SLT) research that is responsive to Māori and honours Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations is essential for achieving equitable health practices and outcomes for all in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ). One way to increase Māori representation and address Māori priorities in SLT research is through research advisory groups. This scoping review explored the characteristics of research advisory groups in SLT research involving adult populations in NZ. Electronic databases (Scopus, ProQuest, PubMed, and Google Scholar), thesis repositories, and websites were searched in January 2026. Eligible literature focussed on adults requiring SLT in NZ, with research teams supported by a research advisory group. Of 4,675 initial results, 4,375 were excluded after title and abstract screening. Once duplicates were removed, 240 records underwent full-text screening. Four articles and two theses were included in this review, representing the work of three research teams (one led by a Māori researcher). Research advisory groups were named rangahau whānau (research family), research whānau (family), or stakeholder advisory group. Māori played an integral role in advising and guiding multiple phases of each study, aligning with responsiveness to Māori. Details of advisory group membership, recruitment, and engagement varied across studies. The inclusion of Māori in research advisory groups can be achieved in SLT research, importantly by both Māori and non-Māori researchers. Recommendations are presented for incorporating research advisory groups in future SLT research, partnering with Māori, and collaboratively striving for meaningful, equitable, and transformative changes for people with communication and swallowing difficulties and their whānau.

titel: MAIDTA: an interpretable attention-based multi-modal model for drug-target affinity prediction

titel: When the Mountains Stop Warming the Plains: Anomalous Winter and Spring Cooling in Southeastern Alberta Linked to Reduced Chinook Activity

titel: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Campus Recreation as Identity Work

titel: Defects, interfaces, and charge transport in functional micro/nano powder systems
zusammenfassung: Micro/nano powders are central to functional materials research, yet their behavior is still commonly interpreted through composition, synthesis strategy, or target application alone. The analysis shows that widely used explanations in powder literature remain incomplete when treated in isolation. titel: Digital compassion fatigue in nurses: an evolutionary concept analysis

titel: KINOTECA: A Navigator of Chemical Datasets with Reported Kinase Inhibitory Activity
zusammenfassung: Protein kinases are the most intensively targeted protein family for small-molecule drugs, and the large volume of inhibitory-assay data reported for them makes the family particularly well suited to data-driven and machine-learning approaches to drug discovery. These data formats are suitable for the direct training of machine learning models, such as activity prediction models. By delivering reconciled, analysis-ready data with its provenance preserved, Kinoteca aims to lower the barrier to reproducible, data-driven kinase drug discovery.

titel: How Green Social Expectations and Social Comparison Shape ESG Adoption in Power Battery Recycling: A Dynamic Analysis of Recycling and Pricing Strategies

zusammenfassung: Large diversified firms seeking to enter eco-friendly markets must decide whether to source essential green components from specialized suppliers or develop comparable components in-house. External sourcing facilitates rapid market entry and avoids costly development, but it creates dependence on a specialized supplier that also competes downstream. Internal development eliminates this dependence and gives the diversified firm greater control over component production but it requires substantial investment and may place the firm at a production cost disadvantage relative to the specialized supplier. Moreover, sustainability reputation spillovers further complicate this make-or-buy dilemma, as participation in the eco-friendly market can generate positive reputational effects across the diversified firm’s broader product portfolio. To examine how these trade-offs and reputation spillovers jointly affect sourcing decisions and supply chain structures, we develop a game-theoretic model in which a specialized supplier serves as both a component provider and a downstream competitor. We identify three equilibrium supply chain structures: external sourcing with upstream–downstream coopetition, internal development with Cournot competition, and internal development leading to the supplier’s exit from the downstream market. A critical insight is the supplier’s dilemma: while moderate reputation benefits create mutually profitable coopetition, sufficiently large benefits trigger the diversified firm’s internalization, eliminating the supply relationship and potentially resulting in its exit from the downstream market. Further analysis shows that a higher supplier marginal production cost affects both the diversified firm’s sourcing decision and the conditions under which supplier market exit can occur, whereas a higher fixed development cost shifts the decision boundary toward external sourcing. Our findings suggest that policies amplifying reputation benefits may induce large firms to replace external sourcing from lower-cost specialized suppliers with higher-cost internal development, displacing specialized green producers and duplicating existing technology investments.

titel: Defect-Aware Transport Descriptors for Electrospun PBI Membranes: A Resource-Efficient Structural Screening Approach for Clean-Technology Applications
zusammenfassung: In heterogeneous fibrous networks, the void fraction measured by displacement porosimetry does not coincide with the fraction accessible to through-plane flow, and classical capillary-based permeability models, which take a single nominal porosity as input, cannot resolve this discrepancy. In the present work, a defect-aware structural framework is developed and applied to a set of 17 electrospun polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes produced in triplicate across a broad processing window, covering fiber diameters from 83 to 174 nm, total porosities from 68 to 85%, and defect fractions from 0 to 52.2% as quantified by Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) image analysis. A defect-corrected effective porosity is introduced as a transport-oriented structural descriptor, defined as the fraction of nominal pore volume remaining accessible to through-plane flow after accounting for the obstruction imposed by morphological irregularities. Starting from this quantity, tortuosity is estimated through three complementary analytical models, Tomadakis, Bruggeman, and Koponen, and the corresponding Kozeny–Carman structural resistance constants are derived. All three models consistently show increasing tortuosity and amplified flow resistance as defect content increases, with model divergence becoming most pronounced below an effective porosity of approximately 65%, identifying a structural threshold beyond which heterogeneous fibrous networks deviate significantly from idealized pore-path descriptions. Experimental Darcy permeability, derived from Gurley air-flow measurements, does not exhibit a statistically significant bivariate correlation with the defect fraction alone (rs = −0.38, p = 0.13), consistent with the multi-factorial nature of macroscopic transport in morphologically complex fibrous media. Kozeny–Carman-derived permeability, computed from the corrected effective porosity, still diverges from the Darcy reference by up to 2.7 orders of magnitude, but the deviation is not random: it varies monotonically with effective porosity and crosses unity at 0.81. This discrepancy is therefore interpreted not as a framework limitation but as a quantitative diagnostic of the structural conditions under which classical capillary-based permeability models become unreliable for heterogeneous electrospun mats. The framework is thus diagnostic rather than predictive: from routine SEM micrographs alone, it delimits the structural regime in which capillary-bundle descriptions lose validity, enabling resource-efficient screening of fibrous membranes for clean-technology applications.

titel: Bioengineered human brain organoids and organ-on-chip platforms for exposure-aware assessment of developmental neurotoxicity induced by general anesthetics and sedatives
zusammenfassung: General anesthetic agents and sedative-hypnotic drugs are essential for fetal, neonatal, pediatric, and intensive care procedures, but their administration can overlap with vulnerable stages of human brain development. Particular attention is given to exposure delivery, measured concentration, gas- or liquid-phase stability, microfluidic flow, matrix properties, maturation stage, recovery interval, and assay scalability. We then organize anesthetic-associated changes into platform-detectable developmental stress modules, including progenitor-zone disruption, altered lineage progression, mitochondrial and oxidative stress, ferroptotic or apoptotic injury, synaptic dysregulation, glial and neuroimmune remodeling, and network dysfunction. We further examine how divergent responses are shaped by drug class, dose, duration, brain-region identity, cellular composition, BBB or immune integration, and model architecture. Finally, we propose susceptibility-informed preclinical risk modeling based on patient-derived or isogenic organoids, multimodal readouts, biomarker anchoring, model benchmarking, and reporting standards. titel: Female song and elaborate female coloration: Comparing signaling traits in tropical versus temperate songbirds
zusammenfassung: Abstract Geographic and gender biases in the history of ornithology have led to missed opportunities, and in some cases, backwards understanding of key evolutionary and behavioral processes. In studies of elaborate coloration and song, female birds have historically been neglected. The main framework for thinking about the evolution of elaborate traits has been sexual selection, whereby competition for mates has led to elaborate coloration and long, complex songs in males. Females have often been ignored or assumed not to change. Here we review current understanding of how these elaborate traits have evolved in temperate versus tropical areas. Ongoing research on orioles, other blackbirds, and all songbirds indicates that female song is much more common than previously thought. Social selection acting on both females and males throughout the year likely played an important role in the original evolution of bird song in both sexes. In many cases, the evolution of sexual dimorphism in both coloration and song is driven by the loss of elaboration in females, rather than the gain of elaboration in males. Accounting for both male and female display traits will lead to a clearer understanding of the evolution of coloration and song, which will also facilitate a more comprehensive understanding of the full scope of topics in avian ecology, evolution, behavior, and conservation.

titel: Post-stroke dysphagia across the care continuum: a full-cycle framework for rehabilitation, supportive care, and community follow-up
zusammenfassung: Post-stroke dysphagia is a common and clinically consequential complication of stroke, associated with aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition, dehydration, impaired functional recovery, mortality, and increased healthcare use. Although acute dysphagia screening and aspiration-risk management are increasingly embedded in organised stroke care, long-term reassessment, discharge transition, caregiver education, community follow-up, and digitally supported continuity of care remain less clearly defined. This Review synthesises current evidence on post-stroke dysphagia management within a full-cycle clinical framework extending from hyperacute screening to long-term community care. High-consensus practices include standardised screening before oral intake, timely escalation to clinical swallowing examination and instrumental assessment in high-risk patients, and early supportive decisions regarding feeding route, hydration, medication administration, positioning, oral hygiene, nutrition support, and pulmonary surveillance. Standard swallowing rehabilitation remains the platform from acute rehabilitation through the subacute phase; targeted exercise, electrical or brain stimulation, respiratory muscle training, and biofeedback are optional phenotype-based intensification modules, not universal treatments. Beyond the inpatient episode, care pathways should specify swallowing status, aspiration risk, diet and fluid recommendations, feeding route, oral-care instructions, warning signs, reassessment timing, responsible services, caregiver support, and escalation rules. Palliative care supports preference-sensitive prognosis, symptom, or feeding decisions; community implementation must address access, caregiver capacity, and loss to follow-up. Future research should move beyond isolated short-term swallowing outcomes and evaluate integrated hospital-home-community models using clinically meaningful endpoints, including pneumonia, nutritional recovery, readmission, mortality, patient-reported outcomes, social participation, and caregiver burden. Managing post-stroke dysphagia as a cross-stage, cross-setting, and multidisciplinary stroke-care problem may improve safety, continuity, and long-term recovery.

titel: Mirror Life and the Case for Adaptive Risk Governance
zusammenfassung: The current conversation regarding the potential for a mirror organism, opposite in chirality to typical life on Earth, presents a unique opportunity for the biosafety and biosecurity policy communities. It allows for meaningful and productive conversation before the technology can create a complete mirror organism. Because of their unusual structure and chemistry, mirror organisms might evade immune systems or survive undetected in the environment, posing atypical concerns that current risk assessment and mitigation systems are not built to manage. Due to a lack of data about how mirror life might interact with living things, this emergent biotechnology presents a case study in how to develop a future policy framework to mitigate novel risks: flexible and adaptable, forward-looking, and ready to act before problems arise. Building on existing proposals for cautious, conditional oversight for mirror life, this commentary advances a proposal for adaptive governance, tiered checkpoints, early warning signals, institutional roles, and international coordination systems that evolve as the science develops. It also argues that with structured risk forecasting, regimented oversight, and shared global norms, it is possible to support responsible scientific innovation while protecting against the risks of mirror life.

titel: Targeted stimulation of face-selective visual cortex at retrieval boosts associative face memory in healthy young adults

titel: From insulin resistance to incretin receptor agonism in the prevention of type 2 diabetes mellitus in obese individuals
zusammenfassung: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents one of the most significant metabolic challenges of the modern era, with more than 828 million people worldwide living with diabetes. In individuals with obesity and insulin resistance, progression through prediabetes to overt hyperglycaemia represents an important, although not universal, disease trajectory and provides a clinically relevant window for preventive intervention.
